## Sequence

The execution portfolio holds the remaining work as bounded units, including the D01 owner-contract checkpoint. The execution guide defines plugin routing, agent write ownership, serial Cargo verification and main-targeted stacked PRs under the existing CI trigger.

### 1. Correct the model in bounded changes

- D01: confirm exact ownership, compatibility, native authority and registry-output proof contracts before architectural code; existing-contract repairs do not wait for it.
- T06 and T06-HISTORY: canonical new references and legacy/history migration across selectors, config, groups, changesets, reports, pre-state and tags. Rename, manifest additions, promotion and demotion retain the right owner's history. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) remains proposed until implementation.
- T07: supported version authority and native distribution representations. Cover co-located Cargo/Maturin with Cargo-owned dynamic Python version and inspect built metadata; do not insert a second static version or build a universal converter.
- T08 and T08-RETRY: shared physical effect ownership, publication/announcement prerequisites and retry selection after a tag exists. Retain the committed roster and no-journal executor. A future Go source tag is publication, not a universal completion marker.
- T09 and T09-ROUTES: declared registry-output inventory, Python partial-file recovery, yank/conflict semantics and private-index routing. Complete only required selected files/platforms, without guessed platform matrices or unapproved checksum/channel policy.

The plan is an implementation portfolio, not an approved future-behavior spec. Resolve wire/compatibility choices and update the matching area spec with implementation; do not treat architectural packets as fully gated implementer handoffs before D01.

### 2. Reconcile generated workflows

T10 derives build/placement rosters from the verified intent. Native lifecycle hooks remain package-owner-defined and outside Callisto's release-operation graph; Callisto does not inspect or alter them.

A native Python argv test does not imply a generated Maturin workflow, authenticated private-index observation or complete wheel-set recovery.

### 3. Verify supported workflows and onboarding

Each implementation unit adds its own regression/fault tests. T12 integrates these representative cases through production/native paths; T12-DX measures onboarding:

| Fixture | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo workspace | Inherited/root versions, renamed dependencies, locked resolution and index propagation |
| npm/pnpm | Workspace ranges, aliases, paths, catalogs, peer/optional/private policy and packed metadata |
| Python | Native versions, extras/markers, prereleases, required wheel/sdist set and partial upload |
| Cargo+napi | Selected target builds, owner-defined lifecycle hooks preserved, Callisto-owned publication ordering and clean install/load |
| Cargo+Maturin | Co-located static/dynamic metadata, native version mapping and wheel metadata |
| Mixed workspace | No unrelated addon builds, foreign-name rewrites or missed affected lockfiles |
| History/retry | Correct ownership through transitions; missing push/forge/assets/files completed with original artifacts |

Retain local real-registry tests and record missing prerequisites as skips. Run `just ci` for implementation handoffs and workflow contract/policy checks for workflow changes. Measure fresh-repo first publication against the owner's ten-minute goal. Go/NuGet examples check model assumptions only; they are not new runtime gates.

- Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only scope, npm channel policy, universal checksum requirements and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only/manual releases: managed PR selection depends on changesets and verification requires a consumed changeset (ADR 2). Decide before broadening authorization.

- npm writes normalize arbitrary JSON layout; decide whether more than key order/indentation/line endings is needed.
- Preserve redacted stderr for indeterminate provider failures; never stream unredacted native-tool output.
- Publish final migration notices for retired callisto-format, callisto-vcs, callisto-conventional and callisto-changelog, naming callisto-model or callisto-graph.

- Pin the floating moon minor in .prototools after checking proto compatibility.

1	# Next work after 0.10.2
2	
3	Baseline: main `07154021c` (release 0.10.2 published 2026-10-14). Written as a handoff: a fresh session should read this file, then only the contracts and code each brief names. Delete a workstream when it ships, and this file when all do.
4	
5	## State of the world
6	
7	- Published: `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto` at 0.10.2 (tags `callisto@0.10.2`, `callisto-{model,manifests,graph}@0.10.2`; GitHub release with three binaries). 0.10.1 was never published; its changes shipped in 0.10.2. `callisto-fixtures` is `publish = false`.
8	- The v1 hardening batch (T01-T05, T10-BINS/AUTH, T11, T02, T03 family, T04 family) is shipped. Open v1 defects are the rows under "Open confirmed defects" in [V1-FINDINGS.md](V1-FINDINGS.md): SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION, SYS-RETRY, SYS-BARRIER, SYS-NAPI, SYS-MATURIN, SYS-PYFILES, SYS-PYROUTES.
9	- Local gate: `just ci` runs about 1,900 tests with line coverage a little above 91% against a 90% gate. Hosted CI is green.
10	- Release process: merging to main refreshes the bot's release PR; its CI runs sit at `action_required` until the owner approves the workflow runs; merging that PR publishes. A failed publish fails before any effect and is recovered by a `workflow_dispatch` of the Release workflow with `release_source_sha` set to the merged release commit.
11	
12	## Rules for every workstream
13	
14	- Read `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic first. Read `docs/adr/README.md` before touching release flow, Git access, publishing or manifest writes. Specs (`docs/specs/*.json`) change in the same PR as behavior; one changeset per user-visible topic, targeting `callisto-cli`; no changeset for pure refactors or tests.
15	- One `just ci` at a time on the machine, run as `env -u FORCE_COLOR just ci` (this shell exports `FORCE_COLOR=3`, which fails two release tests). Read the log's own `exit=` line, not the background-task notice. Never run cargo builds in parallel inside one checkout; parallel lanes use separate worktrees and run their `just ci` serially.
16	- Prove behavior with the real tool wherever a fake could hide the bug. This session's release failed because every test used a fake `gh`. Credentials, auth, registry and forge paths need either a real-tool check or a harness fake that refuses to run exactly as the real tool does.
17	- Write the failing test first and confirm it fails on the old code (stash the fix, run, restore) before claiming the fix. Test with adversarial inputs, not only the case being fixed.
18	- For refactors, the existing tests are not proof for branches no test executes: check coverage of the code being moved (`cargo llvm-cov --workspace --lcov`) and add characterization tests first.
19	- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); each PR must pass `just ci` on its own. Push over SSH (`origin` is `git@github.com:orin-dx/callisto.git`). Never force-push; add a commit or merge instead. No session links in commits or PR bodies. One line per Markdown paragraph.
20	- Worktree sessions reject complex shell: write scripts to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` and run them by literal path, and use `/usr/bin/git`.
21	
22	## Workstreams
23	
24	| ID | Work | Lane | Depends on | Owner decision |
25	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26	| W0 | Cleanup and docs refresh | A | none | none |
27	| W1 | Test debt: apply mixed-routing, real-service credential check | A | none | where the real-service check runs |
28	| W2 | SYS-RETRY: rerun after a failed tag push | B | none | none |
29	| W3 | SYS-PYFILES then SYS-PYROUTES | C | none | yank and conflict semantics |
30	| W4 | S4: redacted provider output | C | W3 | allow-list shape; wire change |
31	| W5 | R3 then SYS-BARRIER | D | none | none |
32	| W6 | R5 then SYS-NAPI | E | none | none |
33	| W7 | R1: `walk.rs::build` stages | F | none | none |
34	| W8 | SYS-MATURIN | G | D01 | version authority model |
35	| W9 | SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION, resolver divergence | G | W2, D01 | canonical reference model |
36	| W10 | Smaller decisions: distinct target declarations, Python dev groups | H | none | both |
37	| W11 | Verification: T12 integration, T12-DX timing, Python hosted publish | I | W2-W9 as they land | credentials and timing run |
38	
39	## Parallelism and stacks
40	
41	Lanes are independent (disjoint files) and can run in separate worktrees at the same time. Inside a lane, PRs are stacked in the order listed.
42	
43	- Lane A (main, independent small PRs): W0, W1.
44	- Lane B: W2. It touches `release_decision.rs` and tag selection, so W9 waits for it.
45	- Lane C: W3 (PYFILES, then PYROUTES), then W4. All in the registry provider; W4 changes the persisted observation wire, so it is its own decision and PR.
46	- Lane D: R3 (moves only, snapshots first), then SYS-BARRIER, both in `release/derive.rs`.
47	- Lane E: R5a (graph `init.rs` tests to a sibling file), R5b (templates), then SYS-NAPI, all in graph `commands/init.rs`.
48	- Lane F: R1, `walk.rs`. W9 should follow it because both touch identity assignment.
49	- Lanes G, H, I wait on owner decisions.
50	
51	Do not run two lanes that edit the same file at once. Cross-lane conflicts: W9 after W2 and R1; W4 after W3; SYS-BARRIER after R3; SYS-NAPI after R5.
52	
53	## Briefs
54	
55	### W0 Cleanup and docs refresh
56	
57	- Delete merged remote branches (`git branch -r --merged origin/main`; the stack and fix branches from the 0.10.x work) and local branches and worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. Look at each before deleting.
58	- Refresh [ROAD-TO-V1.md](ROAD-TO-V1.md): its baseline is `8ef9aa5a4`, Stage 1 (restore the release path) and T01/T11 are shipped, and v0.9 is not the priority any more.
59	- Prune [V1-FINDINGS.md](V1-FINDINGS.md): remove "Implemented locally, awaiting merge" and the v0.9 handoff, keeping open defects and evidence gaps. Verify every row against the code before removing it.
60	- [V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [V1-VERIFICATION.md](V1-VERIFICATION.md) and [V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json): `AGENTS.md` says delete a plan once its work ships. Remove shipped task packets and batch evidence; keep the open ones.
61	- Done when: docs match the code, `just ci` passes (the docs checks), no changeset.
62	
63	### W1 Test debt
64	
65	- Apply mixed-routing characterization. `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` has `write_steps` and `apply_write_step`; the `MixedManifestVersion`, `MixedWorkspaceVersion`, `MixedManifestRewrite`, `MixedWorkspaceRewrite` and `WorkspaceRoot` steps are never executed by any test (confirmed from a line-coverage report). Build a plan where one manifest receives both `Manifest` and `CargoWorkspacePackage`/`CargoWorkspaceDependency` writes (an inherited-version Cargo workspace root that is also a member) and assert the exact bytes and one persist per physical file. The step order must match the pre-refactor loops: batched manifests, workspace roots, mixed-routing versions, mixed-routing rewrites, platform writes, optional dependencies.
66	- Real-service credential check. `runner::tests::the_runner_gives_the_real_gh_its_token` is opt-in (`--ignored`) and needs `GH_TOKEN`, an empty `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `CALLISTO_TEST_ATTESTED_ASSET`. Decide where it runs in CI (the callisto CI workflow, with a downloaded latest-release asset and the job's read-only token) without giving it registry secrets. The release workflow policy script enforces who gets secrets (`.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`); do not weaken it.
67	- Done when: both are in CI or documented as opt-in, each fails against a deliberately broken variant.
68	
69	### W2 SYS-RETRY (rerun after a failed tag push)
70	
71	- Defect, reproduced in the register: `derive_unreleased_decision` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` excludes a package because a local tag exists before the remaining operations are observed. Tag created, push fails, a fresh `callisto release` exits 0 with "Nothing to release." and no receipt.
72	- Contracts: REL-RERUN-02, REL-CMD-01/08 in `docs/specs/release.json`; ADR 2 and 3; `docs/architecture/release.md`. Callisto's own committed-roster CI does not use this path; generated simple CI does.
73	- Approach: selection must observe every operation of a package, not infer completion from a local tag; "nothing to release" only when every operation is observed satisfied. Keep the committed-decision authority intact.
74	- Tests (black box, real binary, release harness in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs`): local tag exists, push fails, rerun publishes the rest and issues a receipt; fully released stays "Nothing to release".
75	- Done when: the reproduction in the register passes, specs updated, changeset ("a rerun after a failed push completes the release").
76	
77	### W3 SYS-PYFILES then SYS-PYROUTES
78	
79	- PYFILES: `provider/registry.rs` returns `Exact` for any matching non-yanked Python file and `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as satisfied, so a partial wheel/sdist upload is adopted as complete. The argv module builds both wheel and sdist. Required outputs must be the full selected file set; PyPI yank is per file (any matching yanked file currently reads as Absent even next to non-yanked files).
80	- PYROUTES: `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload; servers with separate read and upload routes cannot use one override.
81	- Contracts: REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04, `docs/architecture/release.md`, ADR 4; the register's "Integration risks" bullets on completion and yank semantics.
82	- Tests: fault-injected partial upload (the repo's fake-registry harness, `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs` for the real local registry), file-by-file; do not adopt a partial set. Real Python build was never exercised (no network in the audit): run it with real `uv build` if available.
83	- Decision needed: conflict and yank semantics for a partially present set. Do not guess a platform matrix or checksum policy.
84	
85	### W4 S4 redacted provider output
86	
87	- npm observation discards stdout and stderr; an auth failure surfaces as "indeterminate, no details". Add optional `details` to the indeterminate observation, populated from `redact_native_output`.
88	- Code: `provider/registry.rs` (the `transient(...)` call sites), `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs` (`ProviderIndeterminateCause`). The model doc states no arbitrary provider output is persisted; keep it true.
89	- Redaction must be an allow-list, not a deny-list: the receipt is committed, so a miss leaks a credential permanently. Keep a last-resort class (exit code, HTTP status line) so a novel safe failure still gives a signal. Version the allow-list in `docs/specs/release.json`.
90	- This is a persisted wire change: update `callisto schema --type release-receipt` expectations (`schema_guard_test.rs`), the spec, and add a changeset. Test with adversarial inputs (token in a URL, `.npmrc` echo, header line, JSON body) and assert no fixture token appears in any serialized observation.
91	
92	### W5 R3 then SYS-BARRIER
93	
94	- R3: decompose `derive_release_inputs_with` (412 lines, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs`) into selection, remote preparation and operation building, with an `OpIndex` for the four prerequisite maps. Moves only, no reordering of construction: the intent digest covers the operations, so a reorder changes every durable intent.
95	- First add insta snapshots (insta is a workspace dev-dependency) of the serialized intent and the ordered operation-ID list for representative workspaces, then move code. The snapshots must pass unchanged.
96	- SYS-BARRIER (after R3, REL-ORD-01): a dual Cargo/npm owner creates the shared tag and GitHub publication after one distribution's publish but before the other's. Give the owner tag a prerequisite on every required publication (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`). Behavior change: spec, changeset, and a black-box dual-manifest test.
97	
98	### W6 R5 then SYS-NAPI
99	
100	- R5a: move graph `commands/init.rs`'s inline `mod tests` (starts near line 1163 of a 2,459-line file) to `init/tests.rs` (pure move; `callisto-cli`'s init already uses the pattern). Architecture scanners already skip `tests.rs`.
101	- R5b: move the `WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE` and `MATRIX_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE` string consts (around lines 796-1070) to `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/*.tmpl` loaded with `include_str!`, placeholders (`__BRANCH__`, `__COMMIT__`, `__VERSION__`, `__RELEASE_ENV__`) unchanged. Use `.tmpl`, not `.yml`: a placeholder file must not look like a workflow, and `@__COMMIT__` is not a valid `uses:` ref. First pin the exact rendered bytes for both workflow shapes with insta (find the render function from the template consts' callers), then move; also lint the rendered output. The policy and contract scripts consume the generated file.
102	- SYS-NAPI (after R5): generated native builds and placement use workspace-wide napi selection instead of the verified intent, so an unrelated addon can block a Cargo-only release. CLI-WF-04. Derive the roster from the intent; test with a workspace holding an unrelated napi addon.
103	
104	### W7 R1 `walk.rs::build`
105

# Next work after 0.10.2

Baseline: main `07154021c` (release 0.10.2 published 2026-10-14). Written as a handoff: a fresh session should read this file, then only the contracts and code each brief names. Delete a workstream when it ships, and this file when all do.

## State of the world

- Published: `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto` at 0.10.2 (tags `callisto@0.10.2`, `callisto-{model,manifests,graph}@0.10.2`; GitHub release with three binaries). 0.10.1 was never published; its changes shipped in 0.10.2. `callisto-fixtures` is `publish = false`.
- The v1 hardening batch (T01-T05, T10-BINS/AUTH, T11, T02, T03 family, T04 family) is shipped. Open v1 defects are the rows under "Open confirmed defects" in [V1-FINDINGS.md](V1-FINDINGS.md): SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION, SYS-RETRY, SYS-BARRIER, SYS-NAPI, SYS-MATURIN, SYS-PYFILES, SYS-PYROUTES.
- Local gate: `just ci` runs about 1,900 tests with line coverage a little above 91% against a 90% gate. Hosted CI is green.
- Release process: merging to main refreshes the bot's release PR; its CI runs sit at `action_required` until the owner approves the workflow runs; merging that PR publishes. A failed publish fails before any effect and is recovered by a `workflow_dispatch` of the Release workflow with `release_source_sha` set to the merged release commit.

## Rules for every workstream

- Read `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic first. Read `docs/adr/README.md` before touching release flow, Git access, publishing or manifest writes. Specs (`docs/specs/*.json`) change in the same PR as behavior; one changeset per user-visible topic, targeting `callisto-cli`; no changeset for pure refactors or tests.
- One `just ci` at a time on the machine, run as `env -u FORCE_COLOR just ci` (this shell exports `FORCE_COLOR=3`, which fails two release tests). Read the log's own `exit=` line, not the background-task notice. Never run cargo builds in parallel inside one checkout; parallel lanes use separate worktrees and run their `just ci` serially.
- Prove behavior with the real tool wherever a fake could hide the bug. This session's release failed because every test used a fake `gh`. Credentials, auth, registry and forge paths need either a real-tool check or a harness fake that refuses to run exactly as the real tool does.
- Write the failing test first and confirm it fails on the old code (stash the fix, run, restore) before claiming the fix. Test with adversarial inputs, not only the case being fixed.
- For refactors, the existing tests are not proof for branches no test executes: check coverage of the code being moved (`cargo llvm-cov --workspace --lcov`) and add characterization tests first.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); each PR must pass `just ci` on its own. Push over SSH (`origin` is `git@github.com:orin-dx/callisto.git`). Never force-push; add a commit or merge instead. No session links in commits or PR bodies. One line per Markdown paragraph.
- Worktree sessions reject complex shell: write scripts to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` and run them by literal path, and use `/usr/bin/git`.

## Workstreams

| ID | Work | Lane | Depends on | Owner decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W0 | Cleanup and docs refresh | A | none | none |
| W1 | Test debt: apply mixed-routing, real-service credential check | A | none | where the real-service check runs |
| W2 | SYS-RETRY: rerun after a failed tag push | B | none | none |
| W3 | SYS-PYFILES then SYS-PYROUTES | C | none | yank and conflict semantics |
| W4 | S4: redacted provider output | C | W3 | allow-list shape; wire change |
| W5 | R3 then SYS-BARRIER | D | none | none |
| W6 | R5 then SYS-NAPI | E | none | none |
| W7 | R1: `walk.rs::build` stages | F | none | none |
| W8 | SYS-MATURIN | G | D01 | version authority model |
| W9 | SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION, resolver divergence | G | W2, D01 | canonical reference model |
| W10 | Smaller decisions: distinct target declarations, Python dev groups | H | none | both |
| W11 | Verification: T12 integration, T12-DX timing, Python hosted publish | I | W2-W9 as they land | credentials and timing run |

## Parallelism and stacks

Lanes are independent (disjoint files) and can run in separate worktrees at the same time. Inside a lane, PRs are stacked in the order listed.

- Lane A (main, independent small PRs): W0, W1.
- Lane B: W2. It touches `release_decision.rs` and tag selection, so W9 waits for it.
- Lane C: W3 (PYFILES, then PYROUTES), then W4. All in the registry provider; W4 changes the persisted observation wire, so it is its own decision and PR.
- Lane D: R3 (moves only, snapshots first), then SYS-BARRIER, both in `release/derive.rs`.
- Lane E: R5a (graph `init.rs` tests to a sibling file), R5b (templates), then SYS-NAPI, all in graph `commands/init.rs`.
- Lane F: R1, `walk.rs`. W9 should follow it because both touch identity assignment.
- Lanes G, H, I wait on owner decisions.

Do not run two lanes that edit the same file at once. Cross-lane conflicts: W9 after W2 and R1; W4 after W3; SYS-BARRIER after R3; SYS-NAPI after R5.

## Briefs

### W0 Cleanup and docs refresh

- Delete merged remote branches (`git branch -r --merged origin/main`; the stack and fix branches from the 0.10.x work) and local branches and worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. Look at each before deleting.
- Refresh [ROAD-TO-V1.md](ROAD-TO-V1.md): its baseline is `8ef9aa5a4`, Stage 1 (restore the release path) and T01/T11 are shipped, and v0.9 is not the priority any more.
- Prune [V1-FINDINGS.md](V1-FINDINGS.md): remove "Implemented locally, awaiting merge" and the v0.9 handoff, keeping open defects and evidence gaps. Verify every row against the code before removing it.

### W1 Test debt

Build a plan where one manifest receives both `Manifest` and `CargoWorkspacePackage`/`CargoWorkspaceDependency` writes (an inherited-version Cargo workspace root that is also a member) and assert the exact bytes and one persist per physical file. The step order must match the pre-refactor loops: batched manifests, workspace roots, mixed-routing versions, mixed-routing rewrites, platform writes, optional dependencies.
- Real-service credential check. `runner::tests::the_runner_gives_the_real_gh_its_token` is opt-in (`--ignored`) and needs `GH_TOKEN`, an empty `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `CALLISTO_TEST_ATTESTED_ASSET`. Decide where it runs in CI (the callisto CI workflow, with a downloaded latest-release asset and the job's read-only token) without giving it registry secrets. The release workflow policy script enforces who gets secrets (`.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`); do not weaken it.
- Done when: both are in CI or documented as opt-in, each fails against a deliberately broken variant.

### W2 SYS-RETRY (rerun after a failed tag push)

- Defect, reproduced in the register: `derive_unreleased_decision` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` excludes a package because a local tag exists before the remaining operations are observed. Tag created, push fails, a fresh `callisto release` exits 0 with "Nothing to release." and no receipt.
- Contracts: REL-RERUN-02, REL-CMD-01/08 in `docs/specs/release.json`; ADR 2 and 3; `docs/architecture/release.md`. Callisto's own committed-roster CI does not use this path; generated simple CI does.
- Approach: selection must observe every operation of a package, not infer completion from a local tag; "nothing to release" only when every operation is observed satisfied. Keep the committed-decision authority intact.
- Tests (black box, real binary, release harness in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs`): local tag exists, push fails, rerun publishes the rest and issues a receipt; fully released stays "Nothing to release".
- Done when: the reproduction in the register passes, specs updated, changeset ("a rerun after a failed push completes the release").

### W3 SYS-PYFILES then SYS-PYROUTES

- PYFILES: `provider/registry.rs` returns `Exact` for any matching non-yanked Python file and `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as satisfied, so a partial wheel/sdist upload is adopted as complete. The argv module builds both wheel and sdist. Required outputs must be the full selected file set; PyPI yank is per file (any matching yanked file currently reads as Absent even next to non-yanked files).
- PYROUTES: `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload; servers with separate read and upload routes cannot use one override.
- Contracts: REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04, `docs/architecture/release.md`, ADR 4; the register's "Integration risks" bullets on completion and yank semantics.
- Tests: fault-injected partial upload (the repo's fake-registry harness, `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs` for the real local registry), file-by-file; do not adopt a partial set. Real Python build was never exercised (no network in the audit): run it with real `uv build` if available.
- Decision needed: conflict and yank semantics for a partially present set. Do not guess a platform matrix or checksum policy.

### W4 S4 redacted provider output

- npm observation discards stdout and stderr; an auth failure surfaces as "indeterminate, no details". Add optional `details` to the indeterminate observation, populated from `redact_native_output`.
- Code: `provider/registry.rs` (the `transient(...)` call sites), `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs` (`ProviderIndeterminateCause`). The model doc states no arbitrary provider output is persisted; keep it true.
- Redaction must be an allow-list, not a deny-list: the receipt is committed, so a miss leaks a credential permanently. Keep a last-resort class (exit code, HTTP status line) so a novel safe failure still gives a signal. Version the allow-list in `docs/specs/release.json`.
- This is a persisted wire change: update `callisto schema --type release-receipt` expectations (`schema_guard_test.rs`), the spec, and add a changeset. Test with adversarial inputs (token in a URL, `.npmrc` echo, header line, JSON body) and assert no fixture token appears in any serialized observation.

### W5 R3 then SYS-BARRIER

- R3: decompose `derive_release_inputs_with` (412 lines, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs`) into selection, remote preparation and operation building, with an `OpIndex` for the four prerequisite maps. Moves only, no reordering of construction: the intent digest covers the operations, so a reorder changes every durable intent.
- First add insta snapshots (insta is a workspace dev-dependency) of the serialized intent and the ordered operation-ID list for representative workspaces, then move code. The snapshots must pass unchanged.
- SYS-BARRIER (after R3, REL-ORD-01): a dual Cargo/npm owner creates the shared tag and GitHub publication after one distribution's publish but before the other's. Give the owner tag a prerequisite on every required publication (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`). Behavior change: spec, changeset, and a black-box dual-manifest test.

### W6 R5 then SYS-NAPI

- R5a: move graph `commands/init.rs`'s inline `mod tests` (starts near line 1163 of a 2,459-line file) to `init/tests.rs` (pure move; `callisto-cli`'s init already uses the pattern). Architecture scanners already skip `tests.rs`.
- R5b: move the `WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE` and `MATRIX_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE` string consts (around lines 796-1070) to `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/*.tmpl` loaded with `include_str!`, placeholders (`__BRANCH__`, `__COMMIT__`, `__VERSION__`, `__RELEASE_ENV__`) unchanged. Use `.tmpl`, not `.yml`: a placeholder file must not look like a workflow, and `@__COMMIT__` is not a valid `uses:` ref. First pin the exact rendered bytes for both workflow shapes with insta (find the render function from the template consts' callers), then move; also lint the rendered output. The policy and contract scripts consume the generated file.
- SYS-NAPI (after R5): generated native builds and placement use workspace-wide napi selection instead of the verified intent, so an unrelated addon can block a Cargo-only release. CLI-WF-04. Derive the roster from the intent; test with a workspace holding an unrelated napi addon.

### W7 R1 `walk.rs::build`

- `build` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs` is about 590 lines. Stages: discovery, platform owners (already its own function), identity assignment, platform attachment, package resolution with rules, zero-match diagnostics, edge construction.

Needs the owner-contract (D01) decision on version authority before code.

Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
20	- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Proposed decision

- Use canonical slash-qualified distribution references for new exact inputs, authored and generated data; reject new bare and colon-form aliases. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Read existing bare/colon references only through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary with established ownership. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.

## Canonical references and migration

- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

## Prior art and research limits

| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |

Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).

Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Non-goals

No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.

## Canonical references and migration

- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

## Prior art and research limits

| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |

Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).

Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Non-goals

No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

3. **W10:** whether Python dev groups should cascade. My default is yes, but only with a test through the real binary.

Reply with D01 and I'll read the identity, tags and config code and bring back options with trade-offs. Or say "merge" once those PRs land and I'll clean up the worktrees and branches.

1. Exactly which pyproject tables does iter_dependencies read and which does update_dependency_spec write? Confirm groups are untouched. For each: read? written? what happens if a sibling workspace package is listed there.

input.description: Industry research on ownership and PyPI
input.name: research-industry
input.prompt:
Web research task, read-only. Do not edit files. Use WebSearch with mode "extended" for hard or niche facts and WebFetch to read primary sources (official docs, specs, source code on GitHub) rather than blog summaries. Cite a URL for every claim and say which claims you could not confirm from a primary source. Today is 2026-10-15; prefer current behavior and note version numbers.

Context: Callisto is a Rust release-management CLI for polyglot monorepos (Cargo, npm/pnpm, Python/PyPI). Its owner needs to decide three things and wants industry practice, expected behavior and best practice, not opinions.

A. Package identity and release ownership in polyglot or multi-package release tools. How do these represent a package reference in config, changesets/release notes and git tags, and how do they handle (1) the same name in two ecosystems, (2) a rename or move of a package, (3) one release unit publishing several registry outputs (e.g. a Cargo crate plus a PyPI wheel via maturin, or a Rust crate plus napi-rs npm packages), (4) tag naming (per package vs per release unit) and how a tag template change is migrated, (5) migration of old reference formats? Cover at least: changesets (npm), Knope, release-plz, cargo-release, release-please (manifest mode and its component/tag naming), Nx Release, Lerna, semantic-release monorepo plugins, Cargo's own package ID spec (`name@version`, `registry+url#name@ver`), pnpm filters, uv workspaces, and Go module tags for subdirectory modules. Extract: canonical reference grammar each uses, whether a reference carries the ecosystem, how history is preserved across rename, and any known incidents or issues about tag ambiguity or lost history.

B. PyPI multi-file release completion and partial upload. From primary sources (PyPI upload API docs, Warehouse source, PEP 503/592/691/740, packaging.python.org simple repository API, twine and uv publish docs and source): (1) file immutability and re-upload rules (a filename can never be reused, even after delete), (2) what the upload endpoint returns for an existing file (status codes, messages) and how `twine upload --skip-existing` and `uv publish` (including `--check-url` / its idempotent behavior) decide a file already exists and whether they compare hashes, (3) how PyPI exposes per-file hashes and yanked status (JSON API, simple API JSON, PEP 691 fields, `data-yanked`), (4) whether a release with only some files is a normal state (sdist first, wheels later; cibuildwheel flows; trusted-publishing action behavior with `skip-existing`), (5) what other release tools (release-plz, maturin publish --skip-existing, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish, hatch publish, poetry publish --skip-existing, flit) do on retry, and (6) best practice for deciding that a PyPI release is complete and for handling a hash mismatch on an existing filename, and propagation delay between upload and index visibility. Also npm: what `npm publish` returns for an already-published version, and dist-tag behavior on a retry.

C. Python dependency groups. From primary sources: PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`, include-group), how uv, pip (`--group`), PDM, Hatch and Poetry (`[tool.poetry.group.<n>.dependencies]`, legacy `dev-dependencies`) treat them; whether release tools (release-plz, Knope, bump-my-version, python-semantic-release, uv version/uv lock) update workspace-sibling pins inside dev groups; and what uv does for `[tool.uv.sources]` workspace members. Give the expected behavior when a workspace package is released and another member lists it in a dev group (pin vs workspace source vs unpinned).

Return a report under 1800 words, organized A, B, C. For each: what the industry does (table where useful), the expected behavior, best practice, a recommendation for a tool in Callisto's position with the reasoning, and a short list of claims you could not verify. Do not pad.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

## Protocol responses (legacy)

If you receive a JSON message with `type: "shutdown_request"` or `type: "plan_approval_request"`, respond with the matching `_response` type — echo the `request_id`, set `approve` true/false:

```json
{"to": "team-lead", "message": {"type": "shutdown_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": true}}
{"to": "researcher", "message": {"type": "plan_approval_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": false, "feedback": "add error handling"}}
```

Approving shutdown terminates your process. Rejecting plan sends the teammate back to revise. Don't originate `shutdown_request` unless asked. Don't send structured JSON status messages — report progress through your task tools if you have them, otherwise in plain prose.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

anyOf.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

W10b remainder: track groups as Dev edges; about 100 lines of source, 2 files, no wire impact seen.

Model (crates/callisto-model/src/dependency.rs:146): add DepContainer::DependencyGroup(String) and PoetryGroup(String), plus optionally PoetryDevDependencies. DepContainer is #[non_exhaustive] with no serde derive; DepLocator and RewriteKey (cascade.rs:581) have none either. Adding variants is semver-compatible. Unverified: whether durable plans serialize rewrites some other way.

Kind: Dev for every group table. Groups never reach published metadata. Optional would make cascade_action bump the dependent (cascade.rs:46) and add it to require_dependencies_selected (derive.rs:743), causing spurious releases. Dev rewrites only when out of range (versioning.json:105,113). Publish ordering includes Dev for all ecosystems (toposort.rs:109); that is harmless for Python because Dev-only cycles are dropped by PublishEdgeFilter.

Source changes (python.rs):
- Reader, [dependency-groups]: same shape as extras, so reuse requirement_entries with Dev, about 12 lines. It already skips non-string items (python.rs:828), so {include-group = ...} needs no new code.
- Reader, Poetry: extract the loop at :503-555 into poetry_entries(table, container, kind) and call it for the main table, each group table and the legacy dev table. About 15 net lines.
- Writer: replace the container match (:586-619) with requirement_array_mut and poetry_table_mut helpers, and make the match exhaustive. The current `_ => None` at :616 would turn a missed variant into a silent DependencyNotFound. About 30 lines of churn.
- Free with the helpers: [tool.poetry.dev-dependencies] and [tool.uv.dev-dependencies]. Defer pdm, hatch and build-system as recorded follow-ups.
- Lockfile refresh needs no change: active_ecosystems derives Pypi from rewrites (apply.rs:482).

Tests:
- About 8 unit tests in crates/callisto-manifests/src/python/tests.rs: group read, include-group skipped, array write preserving comments and format, Poetry inline and dotted tables, wrong-index not-found.
- About 6 CLI tests in crates/callisto-cli/tests/python_dependency_tables_tests.rs, using the python_workspace helper:
  - an out-of-range group pin is rewritten without bumping the dependent;
  - a covering range is left alone;
  - a bare name is left alone;
  - the same name in a group and an extra is rewritten in both;
  - a Poetry group is rewritten;
  - a dependent that is not released stays unreleased.
- Spec: widen versioning.json:105 and :113.
- Changeset: one callisto-cli patch, written as "Python dependency groups are kept in step when out of range".
- Real-tool proof: run uv lock against a stale workspace group pin (see unknowns).

Edge cases:
- include-group entries are non-strings and skipped, never followed, so there is no cycle risk. uv rejects those cycles itself.
- A name in both a group and an extra gives two edges, because the rewrite key includes kind and locator (cascade.rs:166). Both get rewritten, as the existing runtime+extra test shows.
- Poetry group optional = true only affects install defaults, so tracking is unchanged. Per-dependency optional = true in [tool.poetry.dependencies] is tracked as Runtime today. The cascade outcome is the same, so this is low priority.
- Bare name with [tool.uv.sources] foo = { workspace = true }: the spec becomes "*" (python.rs:837), always covers, and is never rewritten. That is correct. [tool.uv.sources] holds no versions, so it needs no handling.
- Markers and extras on a requirement line are preserved by rewrite_requirement (:857).
- Poetry multi-constraint array form falls to Opaque today, and groups would inherit that.

Unknowns:
- Whether uv lock actually fails on a stale workspace group pin. I expect it does, which would make callisto version fail at the lockfile refresh. Not run; needs a real-uv test.
- Without a workspace source, the stale pin silently resolves the old release from PyPI.
