<teammate-message teammate_id="scope-owner-code" color="blue" summary="Ownership report: options, recommendation, inventory, cases">
Option table and recommendation first, then the rest. All source-derived; nothing was run.

OPTIONS (owner representation)
| | A. Derived owner (Package; owner id = first canonical manifest's ReleasePackageId); collapse shared effects (tag, forge release/publish, uploads) to one op | B. Explicit `owner` in decision entries | C. Owner declared in callisto.toml |
| Wire | Intent 5->6 (op set changes); receipt/envelope bump only if op ids change; decision stays v2 | Decision v3 + new digest transcript; intent 6; receipt/envelope bumps | Config schema; intent 6 as in A |
| Historical breakage | None for committed decisions; old intents already fail with E215 | Committed v1/v2 decisions need an owner-deriving reader, which needs the graph (model crate cannot) | Existing repos must write the table |
| Migration reader | Historical-roster reader for tags/pre.json (needed in every option) | Same, plus decision v1/v2 upgrade | Same, plus declared rename boundary |
| Test surface | derive.rs, intent/simulator, tag + pre-state history tests | A + decision wire tests, schema guard, jq readers in action scripts | A + config resolution tests |
| Size (estimate) | ~10-14 files, 600-900 lines | ~20-25 files, 1200-1800 lines | ~12-16 files, 800-1200 lines |

RECOMMENDATION: A. SYS-OWNER and SYS-DEMOTION live in git history and repo data (bare tags, pre.json keys), not release documents. Every option needs the same fix: read the manifest roster at the tag commit (path, ecosystem, native name) and match the package by current (ecosystem, native name), not by path. B would not fix either finding. A costs no committed-decision migration, reuses existing types (owner constraint, ADR 12), and intents are single-use. Revisit B only if an owner cannot be derived from the graph at plan time. Maturin version authority (SYS-MATURIN, package.rs:56-75, one grammar per package) is a separate change (T07).

SECTION 2, finished. Demotion: cargo/foo@2.0.0 (qualified, newest) and foo@1.0.0 (bare, old). The npm sibling is removed, so cargo/foo becomes Bare("foo"). Its template is foo@{version}, whose glob foo@* misses cargo/foo@2.0.0 (tag.rs:76-81,100). tags.rs:149 picks foo@1.0.0. The bare-to-qualified fallback (tags.rs:172) needs pkg.id.ecosystem().is_some(), so it never runs for a demoted package. Only a hand-written previous-tag-templates helps (tags.rs:158-170). Consequence: version_is_tagged (release_decision.rs:257-273) is false for 2.0.0, so derive_release_roster (:206-215) adds an UnreleasedVersion entry, and commit inference replays from 1.0.0. pre.json is unaffected: a cargo/foo key resolves via identity.resolve (lib.rs:296-307) and moves to foo. What a fix needs: always consider the package's own qualified tags (ecosystem/native name) plus bare tags filtered by the roster-at-commit ownership test, then take the highest version. A genuine rename or move has no git evidence, so it needs an explicit boundary (previous-tag-templates is the precedent).

SECTION 3, inventory (format, reader, committed?, what a compat reader needs)
- Changeset frontmatter `name: severity`: free string; `add` writes display_name (add.rs:40), so bare until promoted. aggregate.rs:296 parses with PackageId::parse (bare, colon, slash accepted), then resolve_id (aggregate.rs:177). Status helpers still use resolve_unique (diverges). Committed. Needs: legacy bare/colon mapped through the identity index; E103 if ambiguous.
- pre.json initialVersions keys: pre_json_key = display_name (lib.rs ~247); old keys bare. assign_promoted_pre_keys (lib.rs:280+) uses sole_owner_at; E245 on no owner. Committed. Needs the roster-at-commit reader.
- callisto.toml: [[package]]/[[package-set]] match (glob over name with optional ecosystem prefix, config/pattern.rs); fixed/linked-group members (Vec<String>, GroupTable::resolve); [release].product-package and [[release.artifact]].package (raw.rs:20-37, IdentityIndex::identifies identity.rs:354). Committed. Needs one exact-ID parser, with globs a separate language.
- tag-template / previous-tag-templates: literal prefix and suffix around {version}; no {name} placeholder (tag.rs:12-45). Default is display_name@. Committed.
- Git tags: foo@x or cargo/foo@x, never renamed. Readers must cover both families.
- .callisto/release-decision.json: entries[].package and Cascade.from are canonical ReleasePackageId (colon rejected, package_id.rs:55). Schema v2, reads 1 and 2 (decision.rs ~100). Digest covers package strings. Committed via release PR.
- Intent v5 (exact match only, intent.rs:43-60), run envelope v3, receipt v2: ReleasePackageId in operation ids, snapshot.packages, artifactSlots. Transient, not committed.
- JSON reports (BumpRecord report.rs:47, StatusPackageRecord report.rs:138, plan.rs:94): PackageId serialized as display_name, schemaVersion 1 (report.rs:9). Read by CI jq. Not committed. A canonical switch changes the strings consumers see.
- release_pr.rs: grep found no package refs; not read in full.

SECTION 4, existing ownership types vs the four concepts
Types: Package (package.rs:13; id, manifests, tag_template), PackageKey (dir of first canonical manifest), PackageId (display/selector), ReleasePackageId (one per canonical manifest, native name, release_decision.rs:27-43), IdentityIndex.native ((eco,name) -> primary PackageId), GroupTable (version coupling only).
Implicit ownership: add_tags (derive.rs ~480-520) loops every ReleasePackageId, but the tag name comes from package.id, so a dual Cargo/npm package gets two Tag ops for one physical tag. add_forge_releases does the same. Tag waits on all publishes (derive.rs:180). release.md says shared ownership "is not yet a separate authority".
- Release owner: implicit (Package + primary manifest), named in no wire doc.
- Distribution: complete (ReleasePackageId).
- Version authority: missing (single grammar per package).
- Release effect: DAG exists, but shared effects are duplicated per distribution.

SECTION 6, adversarial cases
1. Sibling dir move, name unchanged. Repro: crates/foo (Cargo foo) tagged foo@1.0.0; add js/foo (npm foo), promoted; git mv crates/foo crates/foo-core. At the tag, neither current first-manifest path exists, so sole_owner_at returns None and cargo/foo loses its history and replays.
2. New primary manifest in an existing directory. Repro: js/foo (npm foo) tagged foo@1.0.0; add py/foo (pypi foo), promoted; add js/foo/Cargo.toml (name foo). The first canonical manifest becomes js/foo/Cargo.toml, absent at the tag, so None and E245 for pre.json.
3. Promote then demote (section 2).
4. Primary-name change dropping a package out of the `same` filter (tags.rs:176-178, lib.rs:296; walk.rs:245 promotes on primary name only). Not traced to a failure.
5. Genuine rename or directory move (ADR 11 revisit trigger): needs a declared boundary.
6. Remove a canonical manifest.
7. Tag template change, with previous-tag-templates and E101.
8. Same name in two ecosystems: allowed by native_owner; bare is a wildcard in PackageId::matches; aggregate.rs:296 and resolve_unique diverge.
9. Conflicting legacy and canonical pre.json keys (ConflictingPreJsonBaselines).
10. Rerun after the primary manifest changes between plan and execute (sealed intent should make this a non-issue).

UNKNOWNS
- No scenario run; repro outcomes are source-derived and need fixtures.
- derive.rs forge-publish/uploads and the jq readers of .operations[].id.package (Option A impact) not read.
- release_pr.rs not read in full.
- Stale comment: TagTemplate::default_for doc (tag.rs:76) says native name; code uses display_name().
- No data on how many external repos have bare changesets or pre.json keys.

## 1. Publish path
- **Build runs at execute time.** The registry adapter's `publish` runs build then upload inside the effect (`provider/registry.rs:672-695`).
  - `registry_argv::pypi_publish_argv` (`registry_argv.rs:362-405`) builds `python3|python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist/` in the package directory.
  - There is no `uv build` or maturin path. Maturin projects fail discovery with E007 (`docs/publishing.md:97`).
  - `run_build_argv` strips registry credentials (`registry.rs:253-275`).
- **Upload.** `twine upload [--skip-existing] [--repository-url <endpoint>] dist/<normalized>-<version>*`. The glob is literal, with no shell.
  - `--skip-existing` is added only for the default index or the `upload.pypi.org` and `test.pypi.org` warehouses (`registry_argv.rs:331-336`).
  - Env is `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` only (`registry.rs:225-250`).
- **The file set is unknown at plan time.** The intent holds one `RegistryPublish` operation per package and version, with a registry binding of `registryKey` plus a digest (`operation.rs:11-20`, `intent.rs:14-22`). It has no filenames or digests, and wheel names depend on build tags.
- **No sealed manifest.** `ArtifactManifestV1` covers GitHub asset slots only.
  - Its entries must equal `intent.artifact_slots` (`artifact.rs:175-178`).
  - A slot-less intent rejects any manifest (`release_execution.rs:119-123`), so a Python intent has `artifact_manifest_digest = None`.
  - So the "no new wire" shortcut is not available: nothing is sealed.
- **Two latent glob hazards.**
  - `dist/` is never cleaned, so stale files matching the glob are uploaded.
  - Version `1.0` also matches `1.0.1*`.

- **Evidence source.** `curl -sS -i -H 'Accept: …simple.v1+json' <index>/<normalized>/` (`registry.rs:645-665`). The JSON API is not used.

Resend, design and state table first. Paths are under crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/ unless noted. Read-only: nothing edited, no cargo run. `uv` 0.12.19 and `curl` are present; `twine`, `maturin`, `build`, `pypi-server` are not.

DESIGN (smallest correct, no sealed-intent or wire change)
Keep the one aggregate registry-publish operation per package and version. Add a required-files step to the Pypi adapter:
1. Build once, before the pre-effect observation, into a cleaned outdir. Inventory the matching .whl and sdist files with sha256. An empty or mismatched inventory is a typed miette error with a fix.
2. Classify against the inventory S. Read hashes.sha256 and per-file yanked from the index (both are served: testing/fixtures/providers/pypi-simple/found.http).
   - Any S file yanked: Conflict RegistryVersionYanked. The reason already exists in the model but only the simulator uses it (release_simulator.rs:566). This fails before any effect.
   - S subset of non-yanked R: Exact, so the "already published" warning (REL-RERUN-01) still fires.
   - Otherwise: Absent. A partial set is never adopted.
3. Upload an explicit file list instead of the glob. Upload only the S files missing from R. Keep --skip-existing only where twine accepts it. Confirmation after upload retries until S is a subset of R. A digest mismatch on a file this run uploaded is a Conflict.
4. Leave the read-only observe path (used for tagged-on-HEAD listing) version-level. A tag implies an earlier full confirmation. Cargo and npm are untouched.

Why no wire change is possible: the artifact manifest does NOT seal the Python files.
- ArtifactManifestV1 covers GitHub asset slots only. Its roster must equal intent.artifact_slots (callisto-model/src/release/artifact.rs:175-178).
- A slot-less intent (every Python intent) rejects any manifest (release_execution.rs:119-123), so artifact_manifest_digest is None.
- The intent holds only registryKey plus binding digest (operation.rs:11-20). Wheel names depend on build tags, so S is unknowable at plan time and the build runs inside publish (provider/registry.rs:672-695).

Wire, if you want file digests in receipts anyway: ProviderEvidenceV1::RegistryVersion has {version, checksum?, yanked?} (release_observation.rs:25-34) under deny_unknown_fields. Adding a files field means receipt schema 2 to 3, plus schema_guard_test.rs:551-564 and wire-compat.md. Not needed for the design.
A pre-sealed required set would mean intent 5 to 6. Not recommended.

STATE TABLE (S = declared/built set, R = remote files for the version)
| State | Today | Proposed |
| S subset of R, none yanked, digests match | Exact, adopted | Exact, adopted |
| Some of S missing, none yanked | Exact, adopted (the bug: registry.rs:587-607, mod.rs:325) | Absent proof, upload only the missing files |
| Extra same-version files in R | Ignored; Exact if any match | Ignored |
| Same name, different digest | Hashes never read (registry.rs:536-541), so Exact | Conflict for files this run uploaded; name-only on a rerun (decision 2) |
| Some S files yanked | Any matching yanked file gives Absent (registry.rs:593-595); twine runs; confirm fails Unconfirmed after ~30s retry | Conflict before any effect |
| All yanked | Same as above | Conflict |
| Index lag after upload | One visible file gives Exact at once (registry.rs:75-79,127-141); only Absent is retried | Retry until S is a subset of R, else Unconfirmed; rerun adopts |
| 404 | Absent | Absent |
| 5xx / 429 / rate-limited 403 | 5 attempts, 2/4/8/16s backoff (policy.rs:51-58,173-189), then Indeterminate | Unchanged |
| 3xx / 401 / non-JSON body | Settled Indeterminate or MalformedResponse; curl has no -L and no credentials | Unchanged |
On a custom index there is no --skip-existing (registry_argv.rs:331-336), so an existing file returns 409 and the run fails closed but cannot resume. Today's yanked-mixed case uploads the missing file and then fails confirmation, so a rerun is stuck permanently.

3 (rest). WIRE BOUNDARIES
Receipt holds the envelope plus per-operation evidence (execution.rs:343-350). Current versions: receipt 2, envelope 3, intent 5 (wire-compat.md). ProviderIndeterminateCause::RegistryVersionUnverified exists and is unused in production.

4. TEST HARNESS
- Existing fake: shell shims for curl, python and twine (durable_release_e2e_tests.rs:1254-1288). They use one all-or-nothing marker file and hard-assert the exact URL and glob, so there is no per-file faulting. The simulator has no file notion.
- Classifier unit tests use captured found/yanked/absent fixtures (registry/tests.rs:476-510).
- The real-tool test is #![cfg(target_os = "linux")], skips without pypi-server, build or twine, and calls pypi_publish_argv directly, bypassing callisto observation (callisto-cli/tests/release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:1,24-38,424-484). CI installs pypiserver, twine and build in a venv (.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:109-117).
- A callisto binding cannot reach a local test index: bindings reject http:// with no loopback exception (registry_endpoint.rs:69-76), and a None endpoint hardcodes https://pypi.org/simple (registry.rs:519,528). So no real-index test can go through `callisto release execute`.
A real partial-upload test needs:
- A stdlib loopback server speaking the legacy upload API plus PEP 691 JSON, failing after the first file.
- A CommandRunner wrapper at the graph layer that redirects curl and twine to it (ProviderContext::new takes the runner).
- Real build and twine, available in CI only.
A shim-based callisto-cli/tests/pypi_partial_upload_tests.rs with a per-file state directory is feasible now. The plan already names this file.

5. SYS-PYROUTES
- Config: [registries.<n>] kind="pypi" url, or a per-package index override (callisto-model/src/ecosystem.rs:156-159, binding.rs:73-75). It is validated https and credential-free, stored as PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint (binding.rs:93-97). Only its digest is sealed in the intent.
- Observation (registry.rs:650) treats the endpoint as a simple-index root and appends /<project>/.
- Upload (registry.rs:677) passes the same string to --repository-url, which must be an upload URL. For warehouse-style servers these are different URLs.
- To separate them: add an upload-route field to registry config (config/raw.rs, resolve.rs) and a second endpoint on the prepared binding. The binding digest transcript (registry_endpoint.rs:14-25) must include both, emitting the old transcript when the upload route is absent so existing digests don't move.
- No intent or receipt bump is needed; an old binary sees a stale digest. Spec and docs change; no new CLI flags.
- Authenticated reads stay out of scope: curl gets no Twine credentials.

SIZE AND FILES
About 400-600 lines including tests, one PR. Files: registry.rs, registry_argv.rs, registry/tests.rs, error.rs, docs/specs/release.json (REL-PUB-04, REL-PUB-08 plus a new criterion), docs/architecture/release.md, docs/publishing.md, docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md.
Tests:
- A table-driven classifier over the fixtures: S subset of R, missing, yanked, extras, hash mismatch.
- A shim test that fails after the first upload, then reruns.
- A stale-dist case and a "1.0" versus "1.0.1" glob case.
- The Linux-only real test extended to a partial upload.
T09-ROUTES is separate, about 300 lines.

OWNER DECISIONS
1. Is the inventory trusted because this execute run built it from the sealed checkout, with no envelope binding? Recommend yes, since no separate Python build job exists.
2. On a rerun, is a rebuilt file with a different digest a Conflict or an adopted name match? Strict Conflict can strand a resume if builds aren't byte-reproducible. Recommend name-only completeness on a rerun, digest checks only for files this run uploaded.
3. Are extras ignored? Recommend yes.

NOT VERIFIED
- Twine upload order and behaviour after a mid-list failure.
- Whether pypiserver, devpi or Artifactory serve PEP 691 JSON with hashes.
- PyPI simple-index cache-control is max-age=600 (fixture) against the 30s confirmation window.
- Sdist and wheel byte-reproducibility across runners.

- Whether an untracked dist/ dirties the worktree trust check.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="research-industry" color="yellow" summary="Full industry report: A findings 2-5, B, C with sources">
Industry research, resent from A finding 2 onward (A table and finding 1 were in the earlier message). Research date 2026-10-15. Where a claim rests on a secondary source or a search summary, I say so.

## A (continued)

2. One unit, several registry outputs.
- Knope is the closest documented model. One package lists `versioned_files` across ecosystems (Cargo.toml, package.json), and all must carry the same version. https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/
- release-please does the same with `extra-files` (generic/json/xml/yaml/toml updaters). https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/customizing.md
- No tool documents per-registry completion state. Completion tracking is the tool's job, not the config format's.

3. Rename or move, and history.
- Only Go documents it: `Deprecated:` and `retract` in go.mod, old tags kept, v2+ needs a `/vN` path suffix. Subdirectory modules use the directory as the tag prefix (`gopls/v0.1.0`). https://go.dev/ref/mod
- release-plz, cargo-release, release-please, Nx and Changesets docs have no rename text (I searched each).
- These tools find the previous release by scanning tags that match the current pattern, so a rename or pattern change orphans history. That is my inference from how they work. Not a quoted statement.

4. Tag template change.
- No tool doc describes a migration.
- A search summary says release-please ignores old-format tags and re-proposes releases for everything since the manifest version. That is secondary only.
- Nx says to keep `{projectName}` in the pattern so tags stay unique. Nothing on changing it later. https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/release-projects-independently

5. Old reference format migration.
- Cargo's pkgid accepts both `name:ver` and `name@ver` in the grammar, with ambiguity as an error. https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/pkgid-spec.html
- Nx removed the flat `releaseTagPattern*` keys in Nx 23 in favor of a nested `releaseTag` object. That is the one documented format migration. https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json
- release-please's `include-component-in-tag` default is `true` in the current schema. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/main/schemas/config.json
- A release-please-action issue titled "restore include-component-in-tag default (false)" (#888) suggests the default flipped before. I did not read the issue. https://redirect.github.com/googlecloudplatform/release-please-action/issues/888

Known incidents:
- release-please "Duplicate release tag: v2.0.0" happens when `include-component-in-tag` or `component` is missing in a monorepo. Secondary source only.
- pnpm filters match nothing when two packages share a name and no scope is given. https://pnpm.io/filtering
- Knope warns that package names can collide with Go module tag requirements.

Recommendation for Callisto:
- Identity is an opaque, config-defined release unit id. Ecosystem and registry coordinates are attributes of its outputs.
- Tags derive from the unit id. The tag template is recorded in config, with an alias list of old tag patterns so a template change or rename is an explicit migration, not a silent rescan.
- An ambiguous reference is a hard error (Cargo's rule), never a first match.
- Tag once per unit, never per registry artifact.

## B. PyPI multi-file completion

Primary-source facts:
- **Immutability.** "PyPI does not allow for a filename to be reused, even once a project has been deleted and recreated." Deletion is permanent. Yank is the reversible option. https://pypi.org/help/#file-name-reuse
- **Existing file.** The upload API docs do not document response codes (https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/). Warehouse source returns HTTPBadRequest (400). Message: `File already exists (<name>, with blake2_256 hash ...). See ... #file-name-reuse`. For a deleted filename: `This filename was previously used by a file that has since been deleted. Use a different version.` https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/blob/main/warehouse/forklift/legacy.py (read through a summarizer, not verbatim)
- **twine --skip-existing.** It skips on status 409, or on status 400 with "already exist" in the reason or text. `package_is_uploaded` checks the JSON API by filename, for PyPI and TestPyPI only. No hash comparison. https://github.com/pypa/twine/blob/main/twine/commands/upload.py and https://github.com/pypa/twine/blob/main/twine/repository.py
- **uv publish.**
  - After a failed upload it calls `check_existing`, which reads the simple index (`--check-url`) and compares hashes.
  - Same hash returns `AlreadyExists`, treated as success. Different hash is a `HashMismatch` error.
  - The docs say you can retry the exact same command and "existing identical files will be ignored".
  - The source comment accepts a TOCTOU risk.
  - https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-publish/src/lib.rs and https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/package/
- **Other tools on retry.**
  - maturin matches "already exists" (400), plus "updating asset" and "already been taken", and also 409 and 403 "overwrite artifact". It skips only with `--skip-existing`. No hash comparison. https://github.com/PyO3/maturin/blob/main/src/upload.rs
  - poetry `--skip-existing` uses the same status and message matching. No hash comparison. https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/main/src/poetry/publishing/uploader.py
  - hatch lists existing artifacts from the simple API and skips by filename. No flag, no retry. https://github.com/pypa/hatch/blob/master/src/hatch/publish/index.py
  - gh-action-pypi-publish passes `--skip-existing` to twine. Its README says to avoid enabling it where possible, and warns about parallel jobs publishing only part of the dists. https://github.com/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish
- **Hashes and yank exposure.**
  - JSON API: per-file `digests` (sha256, md5, blake2b_256), `yanked`, `yanked_reason`, `upload_time`. https://docs.pypi.org/api/json/
  - Simple API JSON (PEP 691): per-file `hashes`, `yanked` (bool or string reason), `size`, `upload-time`, `provenance` (API 1.3, PEP 740). HTML uses `data-yanked` and `#sha256=` fragments. https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/
  - PEP 592 defines yank per file, intended as a release-level operation. https://peps.python.org/pep-0592/
- **New hard deadline.** Since 2026-07-08, PyPI rejects new files on releases older than 14 days. The error text and a state API are not documented. https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/ A release left incomplete past 14 days can only be fixed with a new version.
- **npm.**
  - Publishing an existing name and version fails, E403 "cannot publish over the previously published versions". https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-publish and https://blog.npmjs.com/post/81614852121/error-code-epublishconflict-and-cannot-publish-over.html
  - Publish sets `latest` unless `--tag` is given. Tags are mutable, versions are not. https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-dist-tag
  - Changesets treats `failed:already-published` as a handled result. https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts
  - A failed duplicate publish not moving dist-tags is not stated in any primary source I read.

Expected behavior and best practice:
- Partial release is a normal, if transient, state: sdist then wheels, or matrix jobs. The action README's partial-upload warning confirms it arises.
- Define complete as every expected filename present with the expected sha256, read from the simple API JSON or the release JSON.
- Re-upload outcomes: remote hash equals local is success. Remote hash differs is a hard stop (filename burned, so yank and bump). Filename absent means upload.
- Only uv does hash checks. twine, maturin and poetry silently skip a mismatching file, which is the hazard to avoid.
- Propagation:
  - A secondary source says the release JSON shows an upload before the simple index does, and the simple index is cached with `max-age=600`. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-python-cli/pull/290 (unverified, secondary)
  - Use bounded retry (roughly 10 to 30 minutes) for visibility. Do not treat non-visibility as upload failure.

Recommendation for Callisto:
- Do not rely on any tool's `--skip-existing`.
- Before upload, read the remote file list and hashes. Upload only absent files.
- Hash match means done. Mismatch is a blocking error with a specific fix.
- After upload, poll until all expected files are visible with matching hashes.
- Persist expected filenames and digests per output.
- Warn on incomplete releases approaching 14 days.
- Do not create the unit tag or mark released until all outputs verify.

## C. Python dependency groups

Primary-source facts:
- PEP 735 is Final (resolved 2024-10-10).
  - `[dependency-groups]` holds PEP 508 strings and `{include-group = "name"}` tables.
  - Group names are normalized.
  - Groups never appear in built metadata.
  - Installing a group does not install the project.
  - Path and editable dependencies are explicitly out of scope.
  - https://peps.python.org/pep-0735/
- pip: `--group [path:]name` since 25.1. No editable paths. https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/
- uv:
  - `dev` group syncs by default, and `default-groups` is configurable.
  - "Development dependencies can have entries in `tool.uv.sources` the same as normal dependencies", including `{ workspace = true }`. Workspace members are always editable.
  - Legacy `tool.uv.dev-dependencies` merges with groups.
  - https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/dependencies/ and https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/
- PDM: uses `[dependency-groups]`. Editable installs are allowed only in dev groups. https://pdm-project.org/latest/usage/dependency/
- Poetry: supports PEP 735 and `[tool.poetry.group.<n>.dependencies]`. https://python-poetry.org/docs/managing-dependencies/
- Hatch: environments can include dependency groups. https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/config/environment/overview/
- Release tools:
  - Knope's `dependency` key is not supported for pyproject.toml. It works for Cargo.toml (including dev-dependencies) and package.json (including devDependencies). https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/
  - python-semantic-release docs say nothing on sibling pins. https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/configuration-guides/monorepos.html

- Cargo analogy: a dev-dependency with path plus version uses the path locally and the version when published. Path-only dev-dependencies are stripped on publish. https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html

Expected behavior when member A is released and member B lists A in a dev group:

| Declaration in B's dev group | Expected |
|---|---|
| `A` with `[tool.uv.sources] A = { workspace = true }` | Leave the source alone. Update a version constraint only if one is present. |
| `A>=1.2.0` (no source) | Update the pin, same as a runtime dependency. |
| bare `A` | No change. |

- Rewrite constraints in `[dependency-groups]`, `include-group` targets and `tool.poetry.group.*`, with format-preserving TOML edits.
- Never touch `workspace = true` entries.
- Refresh uv.lock after any change.

content.text:
The research is done. Two things changed my earlier plan: a real `uv` test disproved one of the groups agent's claims, and the PyPI design needs no wire change. I read the code behind the three main claims myself and they hold. Everything else below is the agents' source reading, not run code.

## D01: ownership and references

**The two history bugs are real.**
- **SYS-OWNER:** `sole_owner_at` (`lib.rs:260`) decides who owns a bare tag by whether the package's current first manifest path existed at the tagged commit. Move a directory, or add a higher-priority manifest to one, and the answer becomes "nobody", so history replays.
- **SYS-DEMOTION:** the qualified-tag fallback (`tags.rs:176`) only runs for a qualified package id. A demoted package is bare, its bare glob `foo@*` already matches the old `foo@1.0.0`, and it never sees the newer `cargo/foo@2.0.0`.
- **Fix:** always consider the package's own qualified tags, include bare tags only where the roster at that commit shows ownership by (ecosystem, native name), then take the highest version.
- **Ownership representation:** I agree with the agent's pick, deriving the owner from the graph. An explicit `owner` field wouldn't fix either bug, because both live in git history. It costs ~600-900 lines against ~1200-1800, and committed decisions stay valid.
- **Wire:** the intent version goes from 5 to 6 only when a dual Cargo/npm package's duplicate tag and forge operations collapse into one.

**Industry practice** (primary sources where cited in the report):
- **Ecosystem in the reference:** no tool puts the ecosystem inside the reference. Cargo qualifies by source, pnpm refuses an ambiguous name, and cross-ecosystem tools key on a user-chosen name or path. So `ecosystem/name` is a departure from the field, which is defensible because Callisto discovers packages from manifests instead of config-declared units.
- **Opaque ids:** the agent suggested config-defined opaque unit ids. I'd decline: ADR 12 rules them out without demonstrated need, and you've already settled the canonical form.
- **Ambiguity:** an ambiguous reference should be a hard error, as in Cargo. That matches decision 1.
- **Renames and tag changes:** no tool detects a rename. Only Go documents a migration path. So a genuine rename or move needs an explicit declared boundary, which `previous-tag-templates` already is.
- **Tags:** one tag per release unit, never per registry output.

**Suggested split:**
1. A history-reader fix, an existing-contract repair that doesn't wait on D01.
2. Collapsing shared effects, which carries the wire bump.

## W3: Python file sets

- **No sealed file set today.** The intent holds no filenames or digests, and the build runs at execute time. The classifier returns Exact if any one non-yanked file matches (`registry.rs:587-607`), so a partial upload is adopted.
- **Design (~400-600 lines, one PR, no wire change):**
  - Build once into a cleaned directory and inventory the files with sha256.
  - Read per-file hashes and yanked state from the index.
  - Classify against that inventory, and upload only the missing files by explicit list.
  - Yanked files in the set are a Conflict before any effect.
- **Industry agrees:** twine, maturin and poetry `--skip-existing` skip by name without comparing hashes. Only `uv publish` checks them.
- **Existing hazards to fix in the same PR:**
  - `dist/` is never cleaned, so stale files get uploaded.
  - The upload glob for `1.0` also matches `1.0.1*`.
- **New fact:** since 2026-07-08 PyPI rejects new files on releases older than 14 days. A rerun after that can't complete, so it needs a clear error.

**Decisions I need from you:**
1. **Trusted inventory:** is it trusted because this execute run built it from the sealed checkout? I recommend yes.
2. **Rerun digest mismatch:** on a rerun, is a rebuilt file with a different digest a Conflict? I recommend name-only completeness on a rerun, with digests checked only for files this run uploaded. Rebuilds aren't guaranteed byte-identical, and a strict check would strand resumes. The agent didn't verify reproducibility.
3. **Extra remote files:** ignore them. I recommend yes.

## W10b: Python dependency groups

- **The groups agent was wrong about uv.** With `{ workspace = true }`, `uv lock` succeeds and ignores a stale version pin, in a dev group or in `[project].dependencies`. Without a workspace source it fails outright instead of silently using PyPI. Dev groups are also never published.
- **Remaining cost:** a stale pin matters mainly for Poetry or pip users with registry-resolved pins, which I haven't tested.
- **If built:** about 100 lines, treated as `Dev` like Cargo and npm, so it rewrites only when out of range and never bumps the dependent.
- **My recommendation:** do it as a small, low-priority PR, for cross-ecosystem consistency. Defer it if you'd rather spend the effort elsewhere.

## Not verified

- Every repro scenario for the two history bugs, which need fixtures.
- Twine's behaviour after a mid-list failure, and whether a real PyPI call is idempotent on identical hashes.
- Changesets' and Lerna's tag formats.
- Whether the groups claim holds for Poetry.

The ownership history fix and W3 touch disjoint files, so they can run in parallel worktrees once you confirm.

content.text:
Yes, on four narrow topics, because each could change a decision you're about to make. The other two open questions aren't worth more time yet.

**Worth doing before we build**

1. **Reproduce the two history bugs with the real binary.**
   - Both are currently source-derived, from reading the code.
   - A real fixture gives us the failing test the fix needs, and it confirms there isn't a third cause (for example the primary-name-change case, which the agent didn't trace).
   - Cost: small.
2. **Check whether Python builds are byte-reproducible.**
   - This decides W3 decision 2, whether a rebuilt file with a different digest is a Conflict on rerun.
   - I can run `uv build` twice locally and compare the sha256 of the sdist and wheel, with and without `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.
   - If they match, strict digest checks on rerun become safe. If not, name-only is the right call.
   - Cost: minutes.
3. **Check the PyPI cache window against our confirmation retry.**
   - The agent's secondary sources say the simple index is cached for 10 minutes (`max-age=600`), but our post-upload confirmation retries only about 30 seconds.
   - If that's true, a correct upload could be reported as unconfirmed.
   - A single `curl -I` against the real index shows the header.
   - Cost: seconds, provided the sandbox allows network access.
4. **Read the parts of the ownership change the agent skipped.**
   - It didn't read `derive.rs`'s forge-publish and upload paths, the CI `jq` readers of `.operations[].id.package`, or `release_pr.rs`.
   - Those decide how big the intent 5 to 6 bump really is, so the ~600-900 line estimate is soft until they're read.
   - Cost: one targeted agent.

**Not worth it now**
- **Twine behaviour after a mid-list failure, and PyPI's reply to an identical-hash re-upload.** Testing either needs TestPyPI credentials. The design avoids depending on both by never relying on `--skip-existing`.
- **Poetry stale-pin behaviour for W10b.** The feature is already low priority, and `poetry` isn't installed here.

Items 1 to 3 are quick and I can run them myself. Item 4 is one read-only agent. Say go and I'll run all four and fold the results into the W3 and ownership decisions.

Three of the four checks are done; the ownership-collapse sizing agent is still running.

**1. Both history bugs reproduce with the real binary.** `callisto status --format json`, `lastReleasedVersion`:

| Step | Package | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tagged `foo@1.0.0`, then an npm package also named `foo` added | `cargo/foo` | `1.0.0` (correct) |
| Cargo directory then moved (`crates/foo` to `crates/foo-core`), name unchanged | `cargo/foo` | `null` (**history lost**) |
| Both promoted, `cargo/foo@2.0.0` tagged newer than bare `foo@1.0.0`, then npm sibling removed | `cargo/foo` becomes `foo` | `1.0.0` (**should be 2.0.0**) |

SYS-OWNER and SYS-DEMOTION are confirmed as real. I kept the fixture script at `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/repro_owner.sh` as the basis for the failing tests.

**2. Python builds are not byte-reproducible**, which settles W3 decision 2. This is one backend, setuptools via `uv build`.
- Without `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, the wheel and the sdist both changed between two builds.
- With it set, the wheel was identical but the sdist still differed.
- So a strict digest check on rerun would reject a legitimate resume. Name-only completeness on a rerun is correct, and digest checks apply only to files uploaded in the same run. That matches my earlier recommendation.

**3. The index cache window is real.** A live request to the PyPI simple index returned `cache-control: max-age=600`.
- Our post-upload confirmation retries for about 30 seconds.
- I did not test whether PyPI purges its cache on upload, so a correct upload could still read as unconfirmed.
- The W3 design should retry for minutes, not seconds, and treat "still not visible" as unconfirmed, never as a failure.

**Still running:** the sizing agent for collapsing the shared tag and forge operations. I'll report its estimate and the list of consumers that would break when it finishes.

The decisions I'm waiting on haven't changed: W3 decisions 1 to 3, the derived-owner option, and whether to build W10b now. Checks 2 and 3 only strengthen my recommendations on the first and third.

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist, but verified correctness and integration gaps remain. [The findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md) records evidence and coverage; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json) track the work. Cargo real-registry tests now exist; they do not establish full production release-path coverage.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- Verified defects in the findings register are fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. Existing real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests are retained, with skipped prerequisites distinguished from executed coverage and production binding/observation paths checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, dual Cargo/npm outputs, and the common co-located Cargo/Maturin version-authority case. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan/build jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

## Out of scope

- Non-GitHub forges (later).
- Moon plugin (replaced by a proto plugin separately).
- Crate consolidation / license split.
- Production Go or NuGet adapters, arbitrary SCM-derived Python version backends, automatic foreign-registry dependency inference and cross-registry atomic rollback.

  execute:
    needs: [plan, build]
    # A skipped build blocks only when the matrix had entries to build.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix == '[]'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: callisto-release-execute, cancel-in-progress: false}
    permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0} # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: napi-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
      - name: Place napi artifacts
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        env:
          NAPI_DIRS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dirs }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          jq -r '.[]' <<< "$NAPI_DIRS" | while IFS= read -r dir; do
            npx --yes --package @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4 napi artifacts --cwd "${dir:-.}" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-artifacts"
          done
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: asset-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets
      - name: Write the artifact manifest
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json"

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA")

            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
        __RELEASE_ENV__

    """
    Check to see if file already exists, and if it's content matches.
    A file is considered to exist if its filename *or* blake2 digest are
    present in a file row in the database.

    Returns:
    - True: This file is a duplicate and all further processing should halt.
    - False: This file exists, but it is not a duplicate.
    - None: This file does not exist.
    """

    file_ = (
        db_session.query(File)
        .filter(
            (File.filename == filename)
            | (File.blake2_256_digest == hashes["blake2_256"])
        )
        .first()
    )

    if file_ is not None:
        return (
            file_.filename == filename
            and file_.sha256_digest == hashes["sha256"]
            and file_.blake2_256_digest == hashes["blake2_256"]
        )

    return None

content.text:
The three decisions are really two questions about where trust in the file set comes from. Reading your own plan and Warehouse's source changed one of my earlier recommendations.

## What W3 decides

A Python release is several files (a wheel and an sdist). Today any one matching file counts as "complete", so a partial upload is adopted and the release is tagged without the rest. The fix needs three answers: who vouches for the set of files, what a rerun does when a file is already there, and what to do about files we didn't expect.

## New facts from the research

- **PyPI is idempotent for identical bytes.** Warehouse's upload code (`legacy.py`) returns plain `200 OK` when the same filename arrives with the same sha256 and blake2 digest. Any other collision returns `400 "File already exists"`. This answers the question the industry agent couldn't. It also explains why `twine --skip-existing` skips by error text and can silently skip a file whose bytes differ.
- **Builds are not reproducible.** My `uv build` test showed this for the wheel and the sdist, so a rebuilt file will usually have different bytes from the one already uploaded.
- **The documented recovery rebuilds.** Recovery is a `workflow_dispatch` of the Release workflow, which is a new run. Its plan and build jobs run again, so original build outputs are gone.
- **Your plan and the agent's design differ.**
  - T09 says "trusted build inventory, envelope binding", meaning a build job produces the files and a sealed manifest, and the execute job verifies against it.
  - The generated workflow already has plan, then build, then execute, but only for napi and GitHub assets. Python is built inside `execute` today.
  - The agent's design keeps building inside `execute`.
  - My earlier "recommend yes" on decision 1 didn't account for the T09 text.

## Decision 1: who vouches for the file set

**Option A: `execute` builds and inventories, and that is trusted.**
- It's about 400-600 lines with no wire change.
- The security argument for moving the build out is weaker than it looks. `execute` already runs project code for Cargo (`build.rs` during `cargo publish`) and npm lifecycle hooks, which ADR 12 explicitly leaves to package owners. The build subprocess does strip a deny-list of credentials. That list doesn't cover OIDC token variables, though, so I wouldn't call it airtight.

**Option B: a build job produces files plus a manifest of names and sha256, and `execute` verifies.**
- It matches T09 and the existing job split.
- It needs the artifact manifest, which today covers GitHub asset slots only, extended to registry outputs. That is a wire change and likely 1,200-2,000 lines.
- It becomes necessary for compiled wheels, where a matrix must declare the set. That arrives with Maturin support (W8).

**My recommendation: A now,** with the inventory behind one type so a manifest can feed it later. The question for you is whether T09's "envelope binding" was a requirement or a sketch.

## Decision 2: a rerun meets a file that's already there

- **Strict:** treat a digest mismatch as a Conflict. With non-reproducible builds, this strands the documented recovery path on perfectly healthy partial uploads.
- **Name-only (recommended):** a present file counts as done. Digests are checked only for files this run uploaded. PyPI keeps that guarantee, since it refuses different bytes under an existing name.
- **Cost:** Callisto doesn't verify the bytes of files from an earlier attempt. If someone else uploaded a same-named file first, we adopt it. We have no original digest to compare, because there is no journal by design.
- **Consequence for the design:** present files must never be re-uploaded, since a rebuilt, differing file gets a 400.

## Decision 3: files on the release that we didn't expect

- **Ignore them (recommended):** extra files are normal. Examples are a stale name from an earlier attempt, a manual upload, or another job's platform wheels. Printing a note in the output costs nothing.
- **Flag them as a Conflict:** this blocks legitimate multi-job setups, and no tool does it.
- **Boundary:** Callisto declares done when its own set is present. Wheels that other jobs are expected to upload are out of scope, as your plan says ("no guessed platform matrices").

## Still unverified

- Twine's behaviour after a mid-list failure.
- Private-index behaviour (pypiserver, devpi, Artifactory). The public PyPI case is the supported one.
- The 14-day new-file rule, which rests on a blog post.

needs input: confirm decision 1 (build inside `execute` now, manifest later), decision 2 (name-only on rerun), and decision 3 (ignore extras).

content.content:
## Historical ownership

For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `sole_owner_at` checks which same-named candidate's first current canonical manifest path exists at the tag's commit; it does not read every historical manifest name. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies that ownership check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner.

This is not complete rename, manifest-addition or demotion support. Removing a sibling can stop lookup of a newer qualified tag, and current paths can misidentify historic bare ownership. Those failures remain tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md); do not infer migration safety from the directory key alone.

fix(graph): keep a package's release history across a directory move, a new primary manifest and a sibling's removal

A bare tag such as `foo@1.0.0` is attributed to a same-named package by whether that package's current first manifest path existed at the tagged commit. After `crates/foo` moved, or after a package gained a higher-priority manifest beside a same-named one, no candidate's path existed, so the package reported no release and replayed its history. Separately, a package demoted by removing its same-named sibling looked only for its bare tags and chose `foo@1.0.0` over a newer `cargo/foo@2.0.0`.

When no candidate's path existed at the commit, ownership now falls back to the manifests that commit contained: the one candidate with a manifest of one of its ecosystems declaring the shared name owns it, and zero or several matches still mean no owner. A package with the default tag template also reads the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families. The same ownership check serves pre-release baselines.

`GitAccess` gains `files_at` and `read_at` for reading a commit's tree and a file in it.

input.content:
Fixes two history bugs found while scoping the release-ownership work. Both reproduce on `main` through the real binary with `callisto status --format json` (`lastReleasedVersion`):

- A same-named npm package is added, then `crates/foo` moves to `crates/foo-core` (name unchanged): `cargo/foo` reports no release and replays its history.
- An npm package gains a Cargo manifest beside a same-named Python package: the package reports no release.
- `cargo/foo@2.0.0` is newer than bare `foo@1.0.0`, then the same-named sibling is removed: the demoted `foo` reports `1.0.0`.

Cause: a bare tag was attributed by whether a candidate's current first manifest path existed at the tagged commit, and a demoted package looked only for bare tags.

What changes:
- When no candidate's path existed at the commit, ownership falls back to the manifests that commit contained. The one candidate with a manifest of one of its ecosystems declaring the shared name owns it. Zero or several matches still mean no owner, as before.
- A package with the default tag template also reads the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.
- The same check serves pre-release baselines.
- `GitAccess` gains `files_at` and `read_at`. Manifest names come from `read_identity`.

Cost: the fallback runs only when the path check finds nothing, once per distinct tag commit. It lists that commit's tree and reads its manifests. The qualified-tag lookup is a prefix scan of the tag list and compiles no glob.

Not covered: a rename or move that also changes the native name leaves no evidence in Git. It still needs `previous-tag-templates`, as the identity note now says. A bare package that never was promoted would adopt qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and name if such tags exist.

Tests: three black-box tests in `identity_promotion_tests` for the three cases above. I confirmed each case fails on `main` with the real binary before writing the fix. `just ci` passes. No wire change.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
Fixes two history bugs found while scoping the release-ownership work. Both reproduce on `main` through the real binary with `callisto status --format json` (`lastReleasedVersion`):

- A same-named npm package is added, then `crates/foo` moves to `crates/foo-core` (name unchanged): `cargo/foo` reports no release and replays its history.
- An npm package gains a Cargo manifest beside a same-named Python package: the package reports no release.
- `cargo/foo@2.0.0` is newer than bare `foo@1.0.0`, then the same-named sibling is removed: the demoted `foo` reports `1.0.0`.

Cause: a bare tag was attributed by whether a candidate's current first manifest path existed at the tagged commit, and a demoted package looked only for bare tags.

What changes:
- When no candidate's path existed at the commit, ownership falls back to the manifests that commit contained. The one candidate with a manifest of one of its ecosystems declaring the shared name owns it. Zero or several matches still mean no owner, as before.
- A package with the default tag template also reads the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.
- The same check serves pre-release baselines.
- `GitAccess` gains `files_at` and `read_at`. Manifest names come from `read_identity`.

Cost: the fallback runs only when the path check finds nothing, once per distinct tag commit. It lists that commit's tree and reads its manifests. The qualified-tag lookup is a prefix scan of the tag list and compiles no glob.

Not covered: a rename or move that also changes the native name leaves no evidence in Git. It still needs `previous-tag-templates`, as the identity note now says. A bare package that never was promoted would adopt qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and name if such tags exist.

Tests: three black-box tests in `identity_promotion_tests` for the three cases above. I confirmed each case fails on `main` with the real binary before writing the fix. `just ci` passes. No wire change.

The recommendation really rests on cost, and the 400-600 line estimate comes from an agent reading code, not from anything I ran. I put it to you as a question for that reason, but I shouldn't have leaned so firmly on A.

**Decision 3 (ignore extra remote files):** Low stakes. The only support is that no tool flags them, which is absence of evidence.

I'd do these next:
1. Run an independent review of #230.

#!/bin/sh
export NO_COLOR=1
BASE=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/15c732d1/tmp/backends
rm -rf "$BASE"; mkdir -p "$BASE"

mk() { # name backend requires extra

$4
EOF
}

packages = ["src/demo"]'
mk flit flit_core.buildapi '"flit_core>=3.9"' ''
mk poetry poetry.core.masonry.api '"poetry-core>=1.9"' ''
mk pdm pdm.backend '"pdm-backend"' ''

[tool.flit.module]

for b in hatchling flit poetry pdm; do

  (cd "$BASE/$b-a" && shasum -a 256 * | sed "s|^|A |")
  (cd "$BASE/$b-b" && shasum -a 256 * | sed "s|^|B |")
done

content.content:
## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, canonical-only new exact references, registry publication before shared tags/public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. Remaining wire shapes and migration rules below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | The owner chose canonical slash-qualified IDs for every new exact reference; reject new bare and colon-form aliases, and read existing forms only through an explicit ownership migration boundary | Specify which historical records remain readable and how migration is surfaced; cover config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy bare key may resolve to an owner that already has a canonical key in the same file | Choose behavior when both keys carry different versions; current `or_insert` keeps the canonical value and silently drops the migrated legacy value |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | The owner chose required Cargo/npm/PyPI publications before a shared tag and public GitHub release; a future Go source tag can itself be a publication | Specify draft creation and upload ordering and prove all required owner outputs complete before public announcement |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Package owners control hook scripts and any effects they initiate; Callisto preserves native behavior and does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks | Settled owner boundary: preserve it in future publisher changes; do not require hook migration or promise that external hook effects are coordinated |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics

Use Git worktrees and native GitHub stacks.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from a dirty shared checkout.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); plain chained PRs targeting a parent branch get no CI because `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` triggers only for PRs targeting `main`. Each PR must pass `just ci` on its own.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.

import re
import subprocess

root = '/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/owner-history/crates'
files = subprocess.run(['grep', '-rl', 'TagIndex::build(', root, '--include=*.rs'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()

        total += count
        print(path.split('crates/')[1], count)

input.content:
fix(graph): match a historical owner by each package's own native name and read history cheaply

The first fallback treated any manifest of a candidate's ecosystems as declaring the shared name. A package with a second manifest under another name (cargo `foo` plus npm `foo-js`) therefore adopted a deleted npm `foo`'s bare tag, and a deleted package's pre-release baseline was adopted too, giving a wrong version. Ownership now requires the candidate's own manifest in an ecosystem to carry the shared name today, from the identity index, and a manifest of that ecosystem to have declared it at the tag's commit. `TagIndex::build` takes the identity index for this.

The fallback listed a commit's whole tree and read every manifest, about 6,000 git calls and 65 seconds for 200 packages and 30 tags. It now greps a commit for manifests mentioning the name and reads only those, about 275 calls and 3 seconds, and a tag that does not point at a commit no longer prints git errors.

input.content:
Fixes two history defects (three reproductions) found while scoping the release-ownership work. All reproduce on `main` through the real binary with `callisto status --format json` (`lastReleasedVersion`):

- A same-named npm package is added, then `crates/foo` moves to `crates/foo-core` (name unchanged): `cargo/foo` reports no release and replays its history.
- An npm package gains a Cargo manifest beside a same-named Python package: the package reports no release.
- `cargo/foo@2.0.0` is newer than bare `foo@1.0.0`, then the same-named sibling is removed: the demoted `foo` reports `1.0.0`.

Cause: a bare tag was attributed by whether a candidate's current first manifest path existed at the tagged commit, and a demoted package looked only for bare tags.

What changes:
- When no candidate's path existed at the commit, ownership asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name there, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, from the identity index. Zero or several matches still mean no owner.
- A package with the default tag template also reads the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.
- The same check serves pre-release baselines.
- `TagIndex::build` takes the workspace's `&IdentityIndex`, which is a breaking API change recorded in the changeset.

An independent adversarial review of the first version found real problems, fixed here with regression tests:
- It matched any manifest of a candidate's ecosystems, so a package with a second manifest under another name adopted a deleted package's tag, and in a pre-release workspace its baseline, producing a wrong version.
- It read every manifest at each tag: 6,215 git calls and 65 s for 200 packages and 30 tags. Now about 275 calls and 3 s (1.7 s on `main`).
- A bare tag pointing at a blob printed git errors.

Not covered:
- A rename or move that also changes the native name leaves no evidence in Git. It still needs `previous-tag-templates`, as the identity note says.
- Identity is the native name plus ecosystem. A new, unrelated package that reuses a name adopts the old qualified tag of that name, as it already adopts old bare tags.

Tests: seven black-box tests in `identity_promotion_tests`. `just ci` passes.

Hosted CI on #230 is still running. After the research round I'm comfortable with most of it. The review of my own work was the most valuable part, because it found real problems.

**#230 (history fix): I'm now comfortable**
- **First version was wrong:** an independent adversarial review found three problems:
  - **Performance:** about 65 s against 1.7 s on a 200-package repo with 30 tags, from roughly 6,000 git calls.
  - **Wrong adoption:** a package with a second manifest under another name adopted a deleted package's tag, and in a pre-release workspace its baseline. That produced `5.1.0-beta.0` for a package at `0.1.0`.
  - **Stderr noise:** git errors printed for a tag pointing at a blob.
- **What I changed:**
  - Ownership now requires the candidate's own manifest to carry the shared name today, taken from the identity index.
  - History is found with `git grep` instead of reading the whole tree.
- **Re-run of the reviewer's repros:** the wrong-baseline and wrong-adoption cases are fixed, the true owner now keeps its history, and the timing is 3.2 s with 275 git calls. `TagIndex::build` now takes the identity index, which is a breaking API change recorded in the changeset.
- **Tests and gate:** there are seven black-box tests, and `just ci` passes.
- **Remaining caveat:** the new `git grep` code has not had its own independent review. I can run a narrower second pass if you want one before merging.

**Collapse of shared effects: comfortable to build**
- **Reproduced:** a dual Cargo/npm product with release artifacts currently fails `release --dry-run` with "release intent repeats an artifact slot" (E158). The collapse fixes a real user-facing bug.
- **Partial selection:** `--package npm/dual` and `--package cargo/dual` each plan fine today, so the owner rule is "first selected identity".
- **Manifest order:** it is deterministic, sorted by a named priority (Cargo, npm, PyPI), not by filesystem.
- **Wire policy:** I read it myself, and "no version bump, stale intents fail closed" is consistent with it.

**W3: better grounded, still your call**
- **Build reproducibility varies by backend:** hatchling and poetry-core are byte-identical across timestamp changes, pdm-backend's wheel is identical but its sdist isn't, and setuptools differs. Name-only on rerun still holds, since Callisto can't assume which backend is used.
- **Twine, from its source:** uploads are sequential and abort at the first non-skippable error, `--skip-existing` skips by name without comparing hashes, and without the flag a rerun is stuck.
- **PyPI re-upload:** Warehouse returns 200 for identical bytes and 400 "File already exists" for different bytes under the same name.
- **Your plan:** the registry-file-set row in `V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md` is an open proposal, not a decided requirement, so building inside `execute` doesn't contradict a settled decision. The plan's phrase "local retries retain original bytes" is the one property my design doesn't provide.
- **My recommendations stay:** decisions 1 to 3 are unchanged.

**W10b: defer**
- uv rejects or ignores version pins for workspace members.
- Poetry has no workspaces. Siblings are normally path dependencies, so there is no version to go stale.
- The evidence for building it is weak. I'd record the limitation in the docs instead.

**Still unverified:**
- PyPI's 14-day rule, which rests on a blog post.
- Whether PyPI purges its index cache on upload.
- Private-index behavior.
- Poetry group behavior (not tested).
