# D01 decision brief

Local only, never PR it. Evidence gathered 2026-10-20 on main `d1f0de357` (v0.11.0) with a real binary, scratch repos and five read-only research passes. Each claim is tagged: reproduced (real binary), source (file read), web (URL). I re-ran two of the reproductions myself (E007 and the bare-tag adoption in D01-D). Scratch repos and scripts: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/` (`maturin/`, `history/`, `refs/`, `wire/`, `verify/`).

## What the plan got wrong

The D01 table in `docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md` was written on 2026-09-26. Against v0.11.0:

| Plan row | Today |
| --- | --- |
| Owner identity: durable owner field vs derivation | Owner is already derived (first release id of the package by priority Cargo, npm, PyPI) and sealed in the intent digest. No field is needed (source: `release/derive.rs:258-295`, `capability.rs:287`) |
| Wire compatibility: new versions for owner/effect shape | Release wire is already canonical-only and strict. Nothing in the current scope needs a bump (reproduced: bare and colon ids give E166) |
| Announcement ordering | Shipped. Registry publishes, then tag, then draft, then uploads, then publish (source: `derive.rs:562-612`, `provider/forge.rs:89-102`) |
| Registry file set, Python destinations | Shipped (#232, #233, #249) |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Settled, nothing to do |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases (`or_insert` drops legacy) | Fixed. Different versions now give E305; equal versions are accepted (reproduced; #222) |
| SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION | No longer reproduce (reproduced S1, S2, S4; #230 added the roster fallback in `history.rs`) |
| Status helpers still use `resolve_unique` | Stale. It is `#[deprecated]` with no production caller |

Genuinely open: Maturin (D01-A), the reference boundary (D01-B), the tag default (D01-C), three residual ownership holes (D01-D) and two small release-graph choices (D01-E).

## D01-A: Maturin and native version authority

Reproduced: a directory holding `Cargo.toml` and a maturin `pyproject.toml` fails `status`, `version`, `snapshot`, `release` and `init` with E007, whether the Python version is dynamic, static, workspace-inherited or Cargo carries a prerelease. A separate-directory layout works, but Cargo and PyPI packages cannot be in a fixed or linked group (E107), so there is no lockstep in any layout. Dynamic Python versions are unsupported everywhere (a pyproject-only dynamic project gives E013). The E007 message lists the two grammars in a nondeterministic order (HashSet).

The plan's premise, "deterministic SemVer to PEP 440 mapping", is wrong. Maturin does not map. It parses the Cargo string directly as a PEP 440 version with `pep440_rs` 0.7.3, the same crate and version as Callisto's lockfile (web: maturin `src/metadata.rs`; reproduced with maturin 1.15.0 `pep517 write-dist-info`). Callisto does not write the Python version, so the question is a validation predicate, not a conversion. Callisto's own pre-release mapper (`format/bump.rs:164-211`) falls back to `.devN` for tags maturin rejects, so the two disagree.

| Cargo version | maturin result | Faithful? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1.2.3-alpha.1`, `-beta.2`, `-rc.1` | `1.2.3a1`, `b2`, `rc1` | yes |
| `-pre.1`, `-c.1`, `-rc.1` | all `rc1` | no, three SemVer versions collapse to one |
| `-dev.1` | `.dev1` | no, sorts below `a1`; SemVer sorts `dev` above `alpha` |
| `-post.1`, `-0`, `-1` | `.post1`, `.post0`, `.post1` | no, a SemVer prerelease becomes a post-release that sorts above the release |
| `-next.0`, `-canary.0`, `-my.tag.0`, snapshot `0.0.0-abc-e7efa2b` | error | unmappable |
| `+build.5` | local version `1.2.3+build.5` | PyPI rejects it; SemVer ignores build metadata |

Also reproduced: a static `project.version = "9.9.9"` next to Cargo `1.2.3` builds `9.9.9` silently. Both `version` and `dynamic = ["version"]` only warns in maturin 1.15 (PEP 621 says error). `uv lock --check` passes after a Cargo bump with a dynamic version. Not verified: a full wheel build and install, maturin before 1.15, release-please, cargo-release, Nx and cargo-dist behavior for Cargo-owned Python versions.

Code that assumes one grammar per package (source): `Package::version_grammar` (`package.rs:44-64`; callers `tags.rs:188`, `snapshot.rs:34`, `init.rs:314,329`), `base_versions` taking the first manifest (`lib.rs:210-234`), single-valued `PlannedBump` and `BumpRecord`, `write_version_guarded` writing one `to` to every manifest (`apply.rs:465-482`), `python::write_version` inserting `project.version` next to `dynamic` (`python.rs:453`), `VersionSource` having no dynamic variant (`manifests/lib.rs:46-49`), commit verification comparing `Version` across grammars (`release_decision.rs:534-541`; `Version` equality includes grammar), group grammar check (`groups.rs:49`). The wire already carries a native `targetVersion` per distribution entry, so no wire change is implied.

Options:

| | Behavior | Cost | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 allow-list, dynamic only | One package, Cargo is the authority. Python version is derived with the same parser as maturin and verified. Accept stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N`. Refuse every other prerelease form, build metadata and snapshots for a co-located PyPI output, before any write. - S5: same with npm removed. Cargo `foo` 0.1.0 reports `foo@5.0.0`.
- S6: native rename of the true owner (`foo` to `foo-core`) while an npm `foo` exists. The lookalike adopts the tag and `foo-core` plans from scratch (`release --dry-run` plans `1.0.0` as unreleased).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

1. D01-D: repair now, no decision needed.
2. D01-E: two small choices; the selection fix is a short PR.
3. D01-A: decide whether Maturin is in the v1 promise. A3's E007 fix is independent of it and small.
4. D01-B and D01-C together: they share the display-id coupling. T06 stays blocked until both.

Dependencies: T06 needs B and C. T06-HISTORY is mostly shipped; what is left is D01-D. T07 needs A. T08's remainder needs the D01-E choices.

| --- | --- | --- |

lastPrompt: What is maturin, tell me more

content.text:
Maturin is a build tool for Python packages written in Rust. It compiles a Rust crate into a Python extension module and packages it as a wheel (`.whl`) or sdist that PyPI accepts.

**Why it exists**
- Python code that needs speed or native libraries is often written in Rust through PyO3 (the Rust-to-Python bindings) or rust-cpython. Examples are `ruff`, `pydantic-core`, `cryptography` and `polars`.
- Maturin is the PEP 517 build backend for those projects. A `pyproject.toml` with `build-backend = "maturin"` lets `pip install` or `uv build` compile the Rust code with no setup.py.
- It also handles other Rust-to-Python shapes: `cffi` and `uniffi` bindings, and plain Rust binaries shipped as wheels. It builds platform-tagged wheels (manylinux, musllinux, macOS universal2, Windows) and can cross-compile.

**Commands**
- `maturin develop` builds and installs into the current virtualenv, which is the inner dev loop.
- `maturin build` produces wheels.
- `maturin publish` uploads them.
- `maturin sdist` produces a source distribution.

**Why it matters for Callisto**
- A maturin project is one directory holding both `Cargo.toml` and `pyproject.toml`. It is one crate that publishes to crates.io and one wheel that publishes to PyPI.
- Maturin's metadata rules:
  - With no `[project]` table, everything comes from `Cargo.toml`.
  - With one, only fields listed in `dynamic` come from Cargo, usually `dynamic = ["version"]`.
  - Either way, the wheel version is the Cargo version.
- That causes the E007 failure I reproduced. Callisto requires one version grammar per package: SemVer for Cargo, PEP 440 for Python. Here the same directory carries both, with Cargo as the real authority.

**How its version handling works (what I verified)**
- Maturin does not convert SemVer to PEP 440. It parses the Cargo version string directly as a PEP 440 version.
  - So `1.2.3-alpha.1` becomes `1.2.3a1`.
  - Forms like `-next.0` fail.
  - `-pre.1`, `-c.1` and `-rc.1` all collapse to `rc1`.
  - `-dev.1` and `-post.1` change the sort order.
  - `+build` metadata gives a version PyPI rejects.
- I confirmed this with maturin 1.15.0's metadata hook only. I did not run a full wheel build or install.

That is why decision A in the brief is a validation allow-list, not a conversion.

lastPrompt: What is pep 440 and pep 517?

content.text:
Both are Python Enhancement Proposals, the standards documents that define how Python packaging works.

**PEP 440: version identification and dependency specification**

It defines what a valid Python package version looks like and how versions compare.

- Form: `[epoch!]release[aN|bN|rcN][.postN][.devN][+local]`.
- Examples:
  - `1.2.3`: a final release.
  - `1.2.3a1`, `1.2.3b2`, `1.2.3rc1`: alpha, beta and release candidate.
  - `1.2.3.post1`: a post-release, which sorts above `1.2.3`.
  - `1.2.3.dev1`: a dev release, which sorts below even `1.2.3a1`.
  - `1.2.3+abc.5`: a local version, for builds that are not public. PyPI rejects these.
- It normalizes spellings, so `alpha`, `c`, `pre` and `preview` become `a`, `rc`, `rc` and `rc`.
- It also defines version specifiers such as `>=1.2,<2` and `~=1.2`.

It differs from SemVer, which uses `1.2.3-alpha.1` and puts all prereleases below the release. PEP 440 has no `-next.0`. It also has post-releases, which SemVer lacks. That mismatch is the root of the Maturin problem: PEP 440 can't represent every SemVer prerelease, and some map to a different sort order.

In Callisto, PEP 440 is the version grammar for PyPI packages, and SemVer is the grammar for Cargo and npm. E007 fires when one package has manifests in both.

**PEP 517: a build-system interface for packaging**

It defines how a frontend (`pip`, `uv`, `build`) asks a build backend to build a package, without relying on `setup.py`.

- `pyproject.toml` declares the backend in a `[build-system]` table:
  ```toml
  [build-system]
  requires = ["maturin>=1,<2"]
  build-backend = "maturin"
  ```
- The frontend installs `requires` into an isolated environment, then calls standard hooks on the backend: `build_wheel`, `build_sdist` and a few metadata hooks.
- That makes the backend swappable: setuptools, hatchling, flit, poetry-core and maturin all implement the same interface.

Maturin is a PEP 517 backend, so `pip install .` or `uv build` on a Rust project just works. The hook I used in the research, `pep517 write-dist-info`, is maturin's command for writing package metadata. It reads `cargo metadata` without compiling, which is how I got maturin's real version output.

content.text:
PEP 440 has a crate. PEP 517 does not really, and calling maturin as a library is possible but a poor fit.

**PEP 440**
- `pep440_rs` (0.7.3 on crates.io) implements versions and specifiers. Callisto already depends on it: `callisto-model` uses it, and its `Cargo.lock` resolves to 0.7.3.
- Maturin's `Cargo.toml` pins the same version, which is why my reproduction matched maturin on every input.
- Related crates: `pep508_rs` (dependency specifiers) and `uv-pep440` (uv's internal copy, versioned 0.0.x and marked internal).

**PEP 517**
- PEP 517 is a runtime protocol, not a data format. A frontend installs the build backend into an isolated Python environment and calls Python hooks such as `build_wheel`. A pure Rust crate can't implement that without running Python.
- `pyproject-toml` (0.13.7) parses `pyproject.toml`, including the `[build-system]` table and `[project]` metadata. Maturin uses it. It reads the declaration but doesn't run builds.
- uv has a PEP 517 frontend, but it is internal to uv and not a reusable crate. I haven't checked its code, so treat that as unverified.

**Calling maturin as a library**
- The `maturin` crate (1.15.0) is published and does have a library target. In principle Callisto could call it directly instead of shelling out.
- I would not rely on it:
  - Its library API is not a documented stable interface, so a minor bump could break us.
  - It pulls in a large dependency tree for a tool Callisto only needs to ask one question: what version will you build?
  - AGENTS.md also says ecosystem tools publish and own their own auth (ADR 4), and the plan keeps Callisto out of build logic.
- For D01-A, the question isn't how to call maturin. Maturin's version rule is already available through `pep440_rs`, which Callisto uses. The allow-list option validates the Cargo version with that crate, and a real `maturin` metadata run would only be a check in tests.

I haven't checked the maturin library's public surface in detail. Say so if you want that before deciding.

content.text:
Noted: `pep440_rs` is the parser for D01-A, and I recorded that in the brief. Callisto computes the expected Python version with `pep440_rs::Version::from_str(cargo_version)`, which matches maturin exactly, and doesn't use its own `.devN` mapper for co-located packages. That also removes the maturin-library question.

One decision remains, and the crate doesn't settle it: which Cargo versions to let through. Parsing the same way as maturin doesn't make the result faithful. I measured these cases with maturin 1.15.0:
- `-pre.1`, `-c.1` and `-rc.1` all become `rc1`. Two distinct Cargo releases would then produce the same PyPI version.
- `-dev.1` and `-post.1` land on the wrong side of the stable release when sorted.
- `+build` metadata gives a version PyPI rejects.

The choice:
- **Strict allow-list (my lean):** accept stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N`, and refuse the rest before any write. Cargo users lose custom pre tags like `next` on co-located packages.
- **Accept anything the crate parses, except local versions:** nothing is refused unnecessarily. But two Cargo versions can collapse to one PyPI version. Callisto's rerun logic treats an already-published matching file as landed, so a second release could look finished without uploading anything. I haven't checked whether the existing hash check would catch that, so I'd treat it as a risk.

Which do you want? The brief leans on the strict allow-list.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::{DepKind, ManifestFormat, ManifestRole, PackageId, VersionGrammar, VersionParseError};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, miette::Diagnostic, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ModelError {
    #[error("path `{path}` is absolute; callisto-model paths are workspace-root-relative")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E001), help("Use a relative path relative to the workspace root."))]
    AbsolutePath { path: PathBuf },

    #[error("path `{path}` is not valid UTF-8; callisto serializes paths into its JSON contract")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E002), help("Ensure all workspace file paths contain valid UTF-8 characters."))]
    NonUtf8Path { path: PathBuf },

    #[error("path `{path}` attempts to traverse outside the workspace root")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E003),
        help("Keep workspace file paths strictly within the workspace directory.")
    )]
    PathTraversal { path: PathBuf },

    #[error("`{raw}` is not a valid 40-character hexadecimal commit sha")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E004), help("Provide a valid full 40-character commit SHA."))]
    InvalidCommitSha { raw: String, reason: String },

    #[error("manifest role {role:?} is not valid for format {format:?}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E005))]
    InvalidRoleForFormat { role: String, format: String },

    #[error("package `{package}` has no canonical manifest; at least one is required")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E006), help("Add a canonical manifest file for the package."))]
    NoCanonicalManifest { package: String },

    #[error("package `{package}` has canonical manifests in disagreeing version grammars ({grammars:?}); its version of record has no single grammar")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E007),
        help("Ensure all manifests for a package use consistent version grammars.")
    )]
    MixedVersionGrammars {
        package: String,
        grammars: Vec<VersionGrammar>,
    },

    #[error("package identity `{raw}` has ecosystem prefix `{prefix}` but no name after it")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E008), help("Include package name after ecosystem prefix."))]
    EmptyNameAfterPrefix { raw: String, prefix: String },

    #[error("manifest path `{path}` has unsupported format")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E009))]
    UnknownManifestFormat { path: PathBuf },
}

impl ModelError {
    pub fn invalid_role_for_format(role: &ManifestRole, format: &ManifestFormat) -> Self {
        ModelError::InvalidRoleForFormat {
            role: format!("{role:?}"),
            format: format!("{format:?}"),
        }
    }

    pub fn no_canonical_manifest(package: &PackageId) -> Self {
        ModelError::NoCanonicalManifest {
            package: package.display_name(),
        }
    }

    pub fn mixed_version_grammars(package: &PackageId, grammars: Vec<VersionGrammar>) -> Self {
        ModelError::MixedVersionGrammars {
            package: package.display_name(),
            grammars,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error, miette::Diagnostic, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ManifestError {
    #[error("failed to read `{path}`: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E010), help("Check file permissions and path validity."))]
    Read { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("failed to write `{path}`: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E011), help("Check write permissions on target directory."))]
    Write { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("`{path}` is not valid {format:?}: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E012), help("Verify manifest syntax formatting."))]
    Parse {
        path: PathBuf,
        format: ManifestFormat,
        message: String,
    },

    #[error("`{path}` has no `{field}` field")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E013), help("Add a `{field}` field to `{}`, or exclude it from workspace discovery.", path.display()))]

    InvalidVersion {
        path: PathBuf,
        raw: String,
        #[source]
        source: VersionParseError,
    },

    #[error("`{path}` inherits `{key}` from the workspace root; write the root manifest instead")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E015), help("Update workspace inheritance key in root manifest."))]
    WorkspaceInherited { path: PathBuf, key: String },

### 1. Correct the model in bounded changes

- D01: confirm exact ownership, compatibility, native authority and registry-output proof contracts before architectural code; existing-contract repairs do not wait for it.
- T06 and T06-HISTORY: canonical new references and legacy/history migration across selectors, config, groups, changesets, reports, pre-state and tags. Rename, manifest additions, promotion and demotion retain the right owner's history. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) remains proposed until implementation.
- T07: supported version authority and native distribution representations. Cover co-located Cargo/Maturin with Cargo-owned dynamic Python version and inspect built metadata; do not insert a second static version or build a universal converter.
- T08: shared physical effect ownership, so one tag, draft, upload or publication referenced by several distributions is executed once. The tag already waits for every registry publish of its package, and a rerun after a failed push completes the release. Retain the committed roster and no-journal executor. A future Go source tag is publication, not a universal completion marker.

entries.description:

# Cargo Manifest Reference on Badges and Maintenance Status

According to the Cargo manifest reference, the `[badges]` section is used for specifying status badges for package registries. Here's what it says about deprecation:

## Deprecation Status

Under the `maintenance` table in `[badges]`, one of the available status options is:

> **`deprecated`**: The maintainer does not recommend using this crate (the description of the crate can describe why, there could be a better solution available or there could be problems with the crate that the author does not want to fix).

## Example Usage

```toml
[badges]
maintenance = { status = "deprecated" }
```

## Important Note

The reference includes this caveat:

> Note: [crates.io](https://crates.io/) previously displayed badges next to a crate on its website, but that functionality has been removed. Packages should place badges in its README file which will be displayed on [crates.io](https://crates.io/) (see [the `readme` field](#the-readme-field)).

So while you can specify a `deprecated` maintenance status in the manifest, the badges are no longer displayed by crates.io itself—they should instead be included in the crate's README file for visibility.

content.content:
# What `cargo yank` Does and Doesn't Do

## What It Does
`cargo yank` **removes a previously published crate's version from the server's index**, preventing it from being selected in new dependency resolutions.

## What It Doesn't Do
- **Does not delete data** — The crate remains available for download via the registry's download link
- **Does not affect existing lockfiles** — Cargo will continue to use yanked versions if they're specified in a pre-existing `Cargo.lock` file
- **Does not affect direct downloads** — Existing lock files or direct downloads are not affected

## Key Behavior
> "Cargo will not use a yanked version for any new project or checkout without a pre-existing lockfile, and will generate an error if there are no longer any compatible versions for your crate."

## Legitimate Use Cases

Crates should only be yanked in **exceptional circumstances**:
- Accidental publishes
- Unintentional SemVer breakages
- Significantly broken and unusable crates

## NOT Recommended For

- **Security vulnerabilities** — [RustSec](https://rustsec.org/) is the preferred, less disruptive mechanism
- **Copyright/licensing/personal data issues** — Simply yanking may not suffice; contact the registry maintainers instead
- **Leaked credentials** — Yanking cannot prevent further spreading since existing lock files and direct downloads are unaffected

## Best Practice Workflow
> "A common workflow is to yank a crate having already published a semver compatible version, to reduce the probability of preventing dependent crates from compiling."

Based on the search results, here's what I found about marking crates deprecated on crates.io:

## Current Deprecation Methods

Setting `badges.maintenance.status = "deprecated"` in Cargo.toml and publishing a version allows crate indexing sites to recognize the crate as deprecated. However, there are limitations with this approach.

## Yank vs. Deprecation

The search results show an ongoing discussion in the Rust community about the differences:

- **Yanking**: Yanking all versions of a crate marks the crates.io page as "this crate has been yanked" and provides an immediate indication that the crate shouldn't be used.

- **Deprecation Badge**: The official Crates.io site doesn't show badges set in Cargo.toml, even though they are part of the spec. Additionally, lib.rs and other indexing sites respect the deprecated status badge and display it (for example, showing the crate name crossed out).

## Current Limitations

crates.io doesn't currently offer any way to mark a crate as "do not use" other than setting the README and description or yanking all versions. The community has requested an official way to mark independent versions or ranges of versions as deprecated with a message, but not as forceful as a yank.

The search results indicate this remains an open feature request rather than an official deprecation feature implemented in 2026.

Yes. crates.io has no real "deprecated" flag, so the practical way is one final release of each retired crate that says so. Nothing is published yet.

**What to mark**

| Retired crate | Latest on crates.io | Merged into |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `callisto-format` | 0.8.0 | `callisto-model` |
| `callisto-vcs` | 0.8.0 | `callisto-model` |
| `callisto-conventional` | 0.8.0 | `callisto-graph` |
| `callisto-changelog` | 0.8.0 | `callisto-graph` |

- Each was last published on 2026-09-21, with about 220–280 downloads and none yanked.
- `callisto-moon` was never on crates.io, so it needs nothing.
- The only crate that depends on any of them is `callisto-conventional` 0.8.0, which uses `callisto-vcs`. It is also on the list.
- Your own plan already lists "final migration notices" for these four as an owner operation. I got the target crates from the repo layout (the old code now lives in `callisto-model` and `callisto-graph`).

**What crates.io supports** (from the Cargo reference and the crates.io discussion; the 2026 status comes from a search summary):
- There is no deprecation flag. A community request for one is still open.
- `[badges] maintenance = { status = "deprecated" }` is valid, and lib.rs-style index sites show it. crates.io itself no longer shows badges.
- What crates.io does show is the description and README, so the notice has to go there.
- `cargo yank` does not fit. The Cargo docs reserve it for accidental, broken or unsafe releases. It blocks new resolution and carries no message, and existing lockfiles ignore it.

**Recommendation**
- Publish 0.8.1 of each, with the 0.8.0 code unchanged.
- Description starts "Deprecated: moved into `callisto-model`".
- Add a README notice that names the successor.
- Add the maintenance badge.
- Don't yank.
- Patch, not minor: anyone on `^0.8` keeps a working build, where a stub 0.9 would remove the API.

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist, but verified correctness and integration gaps remain. [The findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md) records evidence and coverage; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json) track the work. Cargo real-registry tests now exist; they do not establish full production release-path coverage.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- Verified defects in the findings register are fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. Existing real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests are retained, with skipped prerequisites distinguished from executed coverage and production binding/observation paths checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, dual Cargo/npm outputs, and the common co-located Cargo/Maturin version-authority case. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan/build jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

## Out of scope

- Non-GitHub forges (later).
- Moon plugin (replaced by a proto plugin separately).
- Crate consolidation / license split.
- Production Go or NuGet adapters, arbitrary SCM-derived Python version backends, automatic foreign-registry dependency inference and cross-registry atomic rollback.

# Next work after the nested-workspace stack

Baseline: main `308d35a91` (#247). Local only, never PR it. Verified against the code on 2026-10-18; the earlier version of this file (written at 0.10.2) listed work that has since shipped.

## Shipped since the 0.10.2 plan

- W1 apply mixed-routing tests (`apply/tests.rs`, `a_manifest_written_through_both_routes_...`).
- W2 SYS-RETRY: `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of packages tagged on HEAD (`release/local.rs`).
- W3 PYFILES: per-file completeness, partial upload recovery, sealed file sets (#232, #233).
- W5 R3 and SYS-BARRIER: `derive_release_inputs_with` is a staged pipeline; `OpIndex::tag_prerequisites` makes a dual owner's tag wait for both publishes.
- W6 R5 and SYS-NAPI: init tests and templates are out of line; the matrix workflow derives napi builds from the intent.
- W7 R1: `walk.rs::build` is staged (`discover`, `assign_identities`, `resolve_packages`, `build_edges`).
- Cargo, npm, pnpm and uv workspaces below the repo root, strict reads, ignored-file preflight, shallow-clone guard, unreadable changelog (#241-#247).

## In flight

- #249 PYROUTES: `publish-url` on a `pypi` registry.
- #250 docs: drop the shipped T09 and T09-ROUTES plan entries.

## Still open and not blocked

- W0 is done once #250 merges. Branch cleanup finished 2026-10-18: 61 merged branches and 11 worktrees removed. Kept on purpose: `docs/crate-consolidation-plan`, `fix/release-consistency`, `refactor/apply-pipeline`, `test/black-box-gaps`, `fix/pypi-per-file-completeness`, `fix/python-declaration-locators` (local commits not in their merged PR heads), `worktree-wave2-base` (3 commits, no upstream), local-only `backup/`, `fix/stack-*`, `pr/*`, `stack/*`, `work/*` branches, `docs/next-work-plan` (locked worktree) and `main` (62 behind).
- T08 leftover: `link_publish_prerequisites` (`release/derive.rs`) makes a dependent wait on every publish of the dependency package, not only the distribution the edge touches. Over-serializes, never unsafe.

## Blocked on owner decisions

- D01 owner contract: options and leans are in `.claude/plans/D01-DECISIONS.md` (2026-10-20). Maturin (A) is deferred to after v1 (#251; T07 removed from the plan). Still open: B canonical-reference boundary and C default tag (T06), E dual-package selection and plugin barrier. SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION and the pre.json alias drop are fixed (#230, #222). D (bare packages adopt bare tags by name, path-exists branch ignores the declared name) is an existing-contract repair under ADR 11, not blocked. ADR 12 stays Proposed until A to C land.
- W1 real-service credential check: where it runs in CI.
- W4 redacted provider output: allow-list shape and the persisted wire change.
- W10: `RewriteKey` discriminator (public API) and Python dev-group tracking.
- W11 verification (T12, T12-DX): needs credentials and an owner-approved run.
- Inferred-only or manual version releases in managed CI (policy).
- Accepted gap: the version-level PyPI read counts a partial file set as present. Callisto tags only after a confirmed complete publish, so only a hand-made tag can expose it.
- A Cargo workspace nested under a root Cargo workspace is still decided by the root's `members` and `exclude` (agreed with Codex; not changed).

- Read `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the matching `docs/architecture/` topic and `docs/adr/README.md` first.
- One `just ci` at a time, as `env -u FORCE_COLOR just ci`; read the log's own `exit=` line. No parallel cargo builds in one checkout.
- Prove behavior with the real tool; confirm new tests fail on the old behavior.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link`). No force pushes, no session links, one line per Markdown paragraph.
- Worktree sessions: `/usr/bin/git`, plain commands, scripts written to the scratchpad.

The v1 plan is one serial chain, and most of the 1.0 requirement is already met. I checked what I could on the real binary (main at 0.11.0):
- `--help` lists exactly the 8 user commands, and `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` and `filter-plan` are gone.
- `init --yes --versioning independent --workflow` writes a 31-line workflow, under the 40-line target.
- `release --dry-run` prints the full plan on a feature branch.

Remaining plan, after #251:

D01 → T06 → T06-HISTORY → T08 → T12 → T12-DX

| Step | What is left | Blocked on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D01 | Decisions B (canonical-reference boundary), C (default tag) and E (dual-package selection, plugin barrier) | You |
| Ownership repair | Bare packages adopt tags by name, plus two related ownership holes | Nothing |
| T06 | One canonical-reference resolver. This is the largest remaining change: about 24 spec criteria and 400+ fixtures. | B and C |
| T08 | Package-granular selection and the over-serialization leftover. Both change intent digests, so they should land before 1.0. | E |
| T12, T12-DX | Production-path verification, and the first publish from a fresh repo measured against 10 minutes | Credentials, and where the credential check runs |

Small items can run in parallel and don't wait on anything except the registry-kind scope. They are the `GroupTable::from_groups` conflict check, the receipt wording, the `.prototools` moon pin, rustc target facts, and explicit registry kind.

**Decisions only you can make.** Wire and public-API changes are cheapest before 1.0, which is why these come first:
1. B, C and E from the D01 brief.
2. W4: how redacted provider stderr is persisted (a wire change).
3. W10: the `RewriteKey` discriminator (a public API change) and Python dev-group tracking.
4. Whether inferred-only or manual releases are allowed in managed CI.
5. Which crates reach 1.0. Only `callisto-cli` is user-facing, so the library crates could stay 0.x. I couldn't find this decided anywhere.

Private PyPI scope, npm channels, checksums and wrapper bump severity are also open, but they are additive and can follow 1.0.

I can start the ownership repair now. B, C and E are what unblock T06, which is the long pole. I put this plan in `.claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md` (local only).

questions.question: B: How strict should canonical references (`cargo/foo`, `npm/@s/x`, `pypi/name`) be for authored files?

options.label: Split by surface (Recommended)
options.description: Canonical required in config, groups, rules, reports/matrix keys and CLI args; colon rejected everywhere. Changesets and pre.json keep native names and resolve at read time, so @changesets/cli interop (ADR 1) and dual Cargo+npm owners keep working. Medium cost.

options.label: Canonical everywhere + migrate command
options.description: Changesets and pre.json also canonical, with a new `callisto migrate` that rewrites old repos and refuses ambiguity. Auditable, but largest cost and breaks @changesets/cli round-trip.

options.label: Hard break
options.description: Reject every non-canonical form, no migration tool. Simplest model, but this repo's own changesets, groups and 111 bare tags break and users hand-edit.

questions.question: C: What should the default tag template be for new releases?

options.label: Keep `{id}@{version}` (Recommended)
options.description: Bare `foo@1.0.0` while unpromoted, `cargo/foo@1.1.0` once a same-named sibling exists. Existing history keeps resolving; tags stay an output name, not a selector. Fix the stale comment and align E101's spec with the code.

options.label: Always `{eco}/{name}@{version}`
options.description: No namespace flip and no sibling scan, but every repo's next release starts a new tag namespace, tags get longer, and a dual Cargo+npm package needs a rule for which prefix wins.

options.label: Require explicit template
options.description: No default; first release needs a written `tag-template`. No inference, but adds first-release friction against the 10-minute goal.

questions.question: E: What should `--package <one id of a dual Cargo+npm package>` do? Today it plans the shared tag and announcement after only that one publish and can strand the sibling.

options.label: Expand to whole package (Recommended)
options.description: Selecting either identity releases every identity of that package, so the tag and announcement always wait for all publishes. No wire change.

options.label: Reject partial selection
options.description: Error telling the user to select all identities of the package. Explicit, but makes a common selector fail.

questions.question: E: Should a product's public announcement wait for the registry publish and tag of a plugin package whose asset it carries?

options.label: Yes, add the edge (Recommended)
options.description: One added prerequisite so nothing is announced until every output of the release exists. Changes intent shape, so it lands before 1.0.

options.label: No, own publishes only
options.description: Keep today's rule: the announcement waits for the product's own publishes and all uploads, not the plugin's registry publish.

(4) Residual owner decisions as concrete either/or (e.g. persist vs print-only; bounded size; allow-list vs deny-list). (5) What you could not verify. Worktree at origin/main d1f0de357 (v0.11.0): /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/v1-research ; real binary at .../target/debug/callisto. First read AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/adr/README.md and ADRs 3 and 4, docs/specs/REQ-DX-V1.md ('Done when' bullets about real-registry tests and the under-10-minute first-publish goal), docs/projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json tasks T12 and T12-DX, docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md 'Integration risks and evidence gaps', docs/releasing.md, docs/publishing.md, the justfile, .github/workflows/*.yml (especially callisto-ci.yml and the release workflows), crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs and any `just provider-contract` recipe, and the user's feedback memory in /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/memory/feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md (fake-tool tests hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; prove auth/release/registry paths with the real tool).

RULES: read-only. Do NOT run cargo or any build, do NOT edit repo files, no gh writes, no pushes, do NOT publish anything anywhere, do not use any credentials. Scratch under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/r2/verify/ (/usr/bin/git, plain commands, Write tool for scripts; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null). Locally available: docker, uv, node/npm/pnpm via proto/mise, python3, moon/proto; no maturin, no verdaccio (you may use `uv tool run`, `npx`/`pnpm dlx` to fetch tools, in scratch dirs only).

TASK: design and VERIFY feasibility of the v1 evidence plan, without credentials. (1) Inventory exactly what the existing real-tool and local-registry tests cover (cargo local registry? verdaccio? devpi/pypiserver?), which skip when tools are missing, which drive production binding/observation vs bypass it (the findings doc says Cargo and PyPI tests drive publisher argv directly), and what the CI workflow runs vs skips (hosted Linux/macOS/Windows). Cite file:line. (2) What can be proven locally with real tools and a local registry end to end through the production `callisto release` path: for each ecosystem (cargo with a local sparse/directory registry or `cargo-http-registry`/Kellnr/alexandrie via docker or crates; npm with verdaccio via `npx verdaccio` or docker; PyPI with pypiserver/devpi/warehouse-lite via uv tool run or docker) attempt a minimal feasibility check of the REGISTRY SERVER ONLY (can it start, accept an upload with the real client, and be read by the simple-index/sparse protocol Callisto reads?). Note Callisto's binding requires HTTPS for registry endpoints (canonical_registry_url, E126), which rules out plain-http loopback: determine whether a local TLS registry is feasible (mkcert/self-signed CA via env such as SSL_CERT_FILE / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO) or whether a test-only escape hatch would be needed, and what AGENTS.md invariants forbid (no cargo features in shipped crates, runtime-chosen behavior). Do not modify the repo; just report. (3) What genuinely requires real credentials/registries (crates.io, npmjs, PyPI/TestPyPI, GitHub releases with a real token) and the least risky way to run it: TestPyPI, a scratch npm scope, a scratch crate name, a throwaway GitHub repo; the repo policy that only the `execute` job gets registry secrets and no GitHub Environment/reviewer gate may be added (AGENTS.md) - find where in the existing workflows a manually dispatched real-service check could live without violating `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`. Give 2-3 concrete placement options with trade-offs (e.g. workflow_dispatch job in a separate workflow with its own scoped secrets, scheduled nightly, local script run by the owner). (4) T12-DX: how to measure 'fresh repo from `callisto init` to first published release under 10 minutes' reproducibly: a script, what steps are timed (init, add, commit, workflow push, merge release PR, publish), what is excluded, what can be measured locally now (init to release --dry-run on all three ecosystems) vs needs credentials. Actually measure the local part on the real binary in a scratch Cargo repo, an npm repo and a Python repo (use `time`; report seconds per step; Python builds may need network for setuptools - report if blocked). (5) Deliver: a verified evidence matrix (executed vs skipped vs simulated), a proposed T12 scope cut that is honest about what was not proven, the credential-free work that can start now, the work that needs the owner (credentials, placement decision), PR slicing with S/M/L sizes, and what you could not verify. Max ~1600 words, evidence tagged [REPRODUCED]/[SOURCE file:line].

input.description: Research 1.0 mechanics and policy items
input.prompt:
Read-only research for Callisto (Rust release manager for Cargo/npm/PyPI monorepos), heading to a 1.0.0 release. Worktree at origin/main d1f0de357 (v0.11.0): /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/v1-research ; real binary at .../target/debug/callisto. First read AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/adr/README.md (ADR process, what 'Accepted' requires), all ADRs' Status lines, callisto.toml, justfile (check-api and other recipes), .github/workflows/*.yml (how Callisto releases itself), the crate manifests (crates/*/Cargo.toml: licenses, versions, publish flags, metadata), and the changelogs (crates/*/CHANGELOG.md heads).

RULES: read-only. Do NOT run cargo or any build, do NOT edit repo files, no gh writes, no pushes, no publishing. Scratch under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/r2/onedot/ (/usr/bin/git, plain commands, Write tool for scripts; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null).

QUESTIONS (research each with evidence): 
1. Which crates would become 1.0? The five workspace crates: callisto-model (MIT), callisto-manifests, callisto-graph, callisto-cli (FSL-1.1-MIT), callisto-fixtures (dev-only). Which are published to crates.io (check `publish` flags; crates.io has model/manifests/graph/cli), which are user-facing (only the CLI + the GitHub action + JSON schemas + config format are the user contract?), what do library crates expose publicly (pub API surface size; is anything documented as stable?), and what does `just check-api` (cargo semver-checks) gate today? Lay out options: (a) all four at 1.0, (b) CLI 1.0 and libraries stay 0.x or are marked internal/unstable (docs, `#[doc(hidden)]`, README notice), (c) lockstep versioning via fixed group (check callisto.toml groups). What does a fixed group imply for versions today? Note the user-facing contracts that 1.0 would freeze: CLI commands/flags, callisto.toml schema, report JSON schemas (`callisto schema --type`), exit codes/error codes (docs/errors.md), tag formats, wire documents (decision/intent/receipt schema versions), GitHub action inputs. List each contract, its current versioning mechanism, and what 'compatible within 1.x' would need (e.g. a schema version policy; docs/architecture/wire-compat.md). 
2. How would Callisto release itself as 1.0.0: its own flow (changeset `callisto-cli: major`? fixed group semantics, CHANGELOG, the release PR #248 'chore(release): version packages' is open now: inspect it with `gh pr view 248` and `gh pr diff 248` read-only; what will it release?), pre-1.0 semver rules in Callisto's own bump logic (does `major` on 0.x go to 1.0.0 or 0.12? check crates/callisto-model/src/format/bump.rs and versioning spec for 0.x handling), tag naming (`callisto@{version}` for the CLI), what else must happen (ADR 12 acceptance and 'Status: Proposed' lines in other ADRs, docs refresh, README/website claims, action pin docs, install scripts referencing versions). 
3. ADR/doc state: which ADRs are Proposed vs Accepted; which docs carry 'proposed', 'planned', 'not implemented', 'pre-1.0' or 'v0.9' language that would be wrong at 1.0 (grep docs/, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, crate READMEs, action README); list file:line. Also `docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md` is labeled 'proposed v1 design, not current behavior'.
4. Owner-policy items: (a) 'inferred-only or manual version releases in managed CI': explain exactly what ADR 2 and the code do today (commit inference can produce pending bumps while hasChangesets is false; managed release-PR decisions return noop; committed verification requires a consumed changeset) with a reproduction on the real binary in a scratch repo (conventional commits with no changeset: what do `status`, `version --dry-run`, and `release-pr`-style commands show); give options with trade-offs and a recommendation; (b) release-commit provenance (ADR 2 threat model; what is verified: digest, decision/diff agreement; what an attacker with push access can/can't do; is anything cheap and worth doing for 1.0); (c) remaining owner/external items from docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md ('Owner/external operations') and ROAD-TO-V1.md ('Owner decisions').
5. Deliver: a 1.0 checklist split into (i) blocking, (ii) decisions needed from the owner (each as concrete either/or with a recommendation), (iii) post-1.0; with S/M/L sizes; and what you could not verify. Max ~1600 words, evidence tagged [REPRODUCED]/[SOURCE file:line].

OWNER DECISIONS: the default tag stays `{display id}@{version}`; tags are never renamed; no persisted owner ledger; a native rename of the tag owner is handled by explicit `previous-tag-templates`, not inference. The fix below is an existing-contract repair under ADR 11 (which rejected "fall back to {name}@ tags without an ownership check").

TASK: produce an executable plan for the residual historical-ownership defects. Claims to re-verify against the real binary and source: (S3) a package whose own id is BARE adopts a bare `{name}@*` tag by name alone because the ownership fallback in crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs runs only when `pkg.id.ecosystem().is_some()`; e.g. npm `foo` owns `foo@1.0.0`, cargo `foo` 0.1.0 is added never released, npm renamed `bar`: cargo foo then reports lastTag foo@1.0.0 / lastReleasedVersion 1.0.0 (already reproduced once on this binary). (S5) same with the sibling removed. (S6) native rename of the true owner while a lookalike exists. (S7) crates/callisto-graph/src/history.rs sole_owner_at: a candidate whose current first-manifest path exists at the tag commit wins without checking the name that manifest declared then. (G2) pre.json bare key attribution in crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs (assign_promoted_pre_keys / resolve path) with no historical check when no promoted same-named sibling exists. Also check: does the same name-only adoption exist for tags found via `previous-tag-templates`, custom `tag-template`, the demotion branch, and for any other consumer of the tag index (e.g. release candidate selection `derive_unreleased_decision`, `version_is_tagged`, `incomplete_tagged_releases`, changelog baselines, `status`)? Search for structurally identical code (AGENTS.md: sibling defects are in scope).

DELIVER: (1) verified current state with exact repro commands and outputs for each of S3, S5, S6, S7, G2, and note any that no longer reproduce. (2) A concrete design: what exact rule decides ownership for a bare package, how the name check is added to the path-exists branch, how git cost scales (read history.rs, the Rosters cache and GitAccess calls; estimate calls per tag), what happens when no candidate matches (diagnostic vs silent no-history; look at how diagnostics are emitted/ordered and what code to allocate in docs/errors.md), and whether a guard "last released version greater than current version" is sound or would misfire (prereleases, pre mode, version resets). (3) Test plan: each test must fail on the old behavior; point to the existing test files (crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs etc.) and fixture helpers to extend. (4) Spec criteria to amend (docs/specs/workspace.json WS-ID-03/08 etc.; docs/architecture/identity.md lines on historical ownership). (5) PR slicing and S/M/L size. (6) Residual owner decisions as concrete either/or. (7) What you could not verify. Report max ~1500 words, evidence tagged [REPRODUCED]/[SOURCE file:line].

  ## Callisto Rust 1.0 readiness audit (read-only; origin/main d1f0de357, v0.11.0)
  
  All four libraries are already on crates.io at 0.11.0, so a semver baseline exists. No cargo build, test or clippy was run. `cargo machete` and `cargo package --list --offline` were the only tools executed. Unverified or from-memory items are tagged [mem].
  
  ### Established facts and sources
  
  - **Current stable is Rust 1.99.1 (2026-10-15)**, preceded by 1.99.0 (2026-10-01), 1.98.x and 1.97.x. Source: [RELEASES.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/master/RELEASES.md). This machine has cargo/rustc 1.98.1.
  - **Edition 2024** shipped in 1.85 ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/02/20/Rust-1.85.0/), [edition guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/index.html)). It makes `resolver = "3"` the default and `cargo new` generates it. Resolver 3 flips `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions` from `allow` to `fallback`, so dependency selection prefers versions compatible with your `rust-version` ([resolver docs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/resolver.html)). Let-chains are edition-2024-only; they stabilized around 1.88 [mem].
  - **`cargo publish --workspace`** (also `-p` and `--exclude`) is stable since 1.90. It publishes in dependency order and verifies by building the whole set as if published, including under `--dry-run`. It is still not atomic ([1.90 blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/09/18/Rust-1.90.0/), [cargo-publish](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-publish.html)).
  - **Trusted Publishing for crates.io** is GitHub-Actions-only. The first release must be published manually. The job needs `id-token: write`. `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1` exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived token and revokes it in its post step ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07), [action](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action)). Search snippets also mention an `environment:` requirement and a 30-minute token ([forge docs](https://forge.rust-lang.org/infra/docs/trusted-publishing.html)). I could not fetch crates.io's own docs page, so confirm the environment rule there before relying on it.
  - **MSRV guidance:** `rust-version` is advisory plus resolver input. Recommended policies are N-2, even releases, or calendar-based. MSRV should be verified in CI with `cargo-msrv`, `cargo-hack` or `cargo +<ver>`. Changing it is a "minor incompatibility" ([rust-version](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/rust-version.html)).
  - **cargo-semver-checks** has a GitHub Action `obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action@v2`. It supports `--baseline-rev` and a workspace lint config, and it does not catch everything ([repo](https://github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks)).
  - **Latest crates.io versions** (API, 2026-10-20): thiserror 2.0.21, toml 1.1.8, toml_edit 0.25.17, petgraph 0.8.3, schemars 1.2.3, rstest 0.28.0, dialoguer 0.12.0, comfy-table 8.0.1, similar 3.2.0, yaml-rust2 0.13.0, clap 4.6.7, miette 7.6.0, jsonschema 0.59.0 (e.g. [thiserror](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/thiserror)).
  
  ### MSRV / edition / toolchain recommendation
  
  | Setting | Now | Recommend |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | edition | 2021 (`Cargo.toml:4`) | **2024** for workspace and `fuzz/Cargo.toml`. Run `cargo fix --edition` and expect `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` and tail-expression-temporary churn. The change is internal to binaries and not semver-visible. Do it before 1.0 so 1.0 is not edition-stale. |
  | resolver | `"2"` explicit (`Cargo.toml:2`) | Drop the line or set `"3"`; 2024 implies it. |
  | rust-version | 1.96 in `[workspace.package]` only | State an N-2 policy. At today's stable (1.99) that is **1.97**, or keep 1.96 only if CI proves it. Edition 2024 needs 1.85, so the floor is not constrained by the edition. |
  | toolchain | `channel = "stable"` (`rust-toolchain.toml`) | Fine for dev. Add a separate MSRV CI job; today the floor is never tested. |
  
  ### Ranked gaps
  
  **Must-fix before 1.0**
  
  1. **Per-crate metadata is not inherited.**
     - Evidence: `crates/*/Cargo.toml` set only `edition.workspace` and `repository.workspace`. `rust-version`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords` and `categories` exist only in `[workspace.package]` (`Cargo.toml:5-12`) and are never inherited.
     - Impact: published crates carry no `rust-version`, so Cargo's MSRV-aware resolution cannot help consumers, and the crates have no keywords, categories or docs link.
     - Fix: add `rust-version.workspace = true`, `keywords.workspace = true`, `categories.workspace = true` and `homepage.workspace = true` to every crate. Per-crate `documentation` should be docs.rs, not `docs.rs/callisto-cli` (workspace-level `documentation` is wrong for the libraries). Effort S.
  
  2. **MSRV is declared but never verified.**
     - Evidence: `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` has no MSRV job, and `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `stable`. The lockfile holds fresh majors (`syn` 3.0.3, `winnow` 1.0.4, `toml_edit` 0.25) whose MSRVs are unknown.
     - Impact: the 1.96 claim may be false, and users on that toolchain would find out at install time.
     - Fix: add a CI job `cargo +<msrv> check --workspace --locked`, and optionally `cargo hack check --rust-version` ([mem] for cargo-hack syntax). Also run `cargo install callisto-cli --locked` in a smoke test. Effort S.
  
  3. **No semver gate, and the public API surface is enormous.**
     - Evidence: `just check-api` exists (`justfile`) but CI never calls it. All modules are `pub mod` in `crates/callisto-model/src/lib.rs`, `callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` and `callisto-cli/src/lib.rs`.
     - Counts of `pub` items: model 514, graph 357, cli 107, manifests 69. `callisto-cli` is a binary whose library target is fully public.
     - Impact: 1.0 on the libraries commits you to a SemVer promise over roughly 1000 pub items. That is likely not intended; the product is the CLI.
     - Fix: decide per crate.
       - Option A: ship 1.0 for the CLI only. Mark graph, manifests and model as "internal, 0.x" in their READMEs, or hide modules with `pub(crate)` / `#[doc(hidden)]`.
       - Option B: audit pub surface down to a deliberate API.
       - Either way, add `cargo-semver-checks-action` to PR CI against the crates.io baseline. Effort M to L.
  
  4. **`#[non_exhaustive]` coverage is uneven.**
     - Evidence: model 44, graph 6, cli 1, manifests 0 occurrences. Public error enums in manifests and cli may lack it. `ModelError` has it (`crates/callisto-model/src/error.rs:5`).
     - Impact: adding a variant or field becomes a major bump.
     - Fix: apply to every public error and report enum, and to option structs with public fields, or prove internal-only via item 3. Effort S to M.
  
  5. **Release publishes with a long-lived token.**
     - Evidence: `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}` in `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (execute job).
     - Impact: Trusted Publishing is the current best practice and removes a stored secret.
     - Fix: configure trusted publishing on crates.io for each crate, and have the `execute` job request `id-token: write`. AGENTS.md and `SECURITY.md` say the token reaches only `execute`; that scope is preserved because OIDC is also scoped to that job. That policy is enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`, which needs updating, and the `environment:` rule must be reconciled with the "no GitHub Environment" owner policy (verify first, see facts above). Moving to OIDC is an owner-policy decision. Effort M.
  
  6. **Library READMEs are stubs with broken links.**
     - Evidence: the four READMEs are 3 to 4 lines each. They link `../../ARCHITECTURE.md`, which 404s on crates.io and docs.rs.
     - Impact: the crates.io page is poor, and `callisto-model` (MIT) has no usage example.
     - Fix: absolute GitHub URLs, an install line, a minimal example, and a stability note. Effort S.
  
  7. **Packaged contents are unfiltered.**
     - Evidence: `cargo package --list` shows 43 test files, `proptest-regressions` and a 64-70 KB CHANGELOG shipped in cli, graph and model. `callisto-cli` also ships `Cargo.lock`. No `include` or `exclude` appears in any manifest.
     - Fix: add `exclude = ["tests/", "proptest-regressions/"]`, or an `include` allowlist, to each crate. Keep CHANGELOG and README. Effort S.
  
  **Should-fix / nice-to-have**
  
  8. **Panic hygiene is not enforced.**
     - Evidence: `Cargo.toml:41-42` explicitly set `unwrap_used = "allow"` and `expect_used = "allow"`. A rough non-test count (cut at the first `#[cfg(test)]`; approximate): about 66 `unwrap` (model 24, graph 40, cli 2), about 48 `expect`, and about 9 `panic!`-family. Examples are `callisto-graph/src/toposort.rs:65-83` (invariant-protected) and `callisto-cli/src/runner.rs:354-355` (piped stdout/stderr, safe).
     - Fix: switch both lints to `warn` in non-test code, use `#[cfg_attr(test, allow(...))]` or `clippy.toml` with `allow-unwrap-in-tests = true` [mem], and convert the rest to `Result` or `let ... else`. A CLI that handles untrusted manifests should not panic. Effort M.
  
  9. **No rustdoc enforcement.**
     - Evidence: no `missing_docs` anywhere. The `pub mod` lists have no doc comments, though doc-comment density in the crates is decent. `just doc-check` runs with `-D warnings` and is in CI.
     - Fix: `#![warn(missing_docs)]` per library, plus `[package.metadata.docs.rs]` if needed. Not required for the CLI binary. Effort M.
  
  10. **Dependency lag and duplicates.**
      - Evidence: thiserror 1, toml 0.8, toml_edit 0.22, petgraph 0.6, schemars 0.8, rstest 0.23 against the latest in the facts list. `Cargo.lock` carries three `toml_edit` versions (0.22, 0.23, 0.25) and duplicate `console`, `anstream`, `syn`, `winnow` and `windows-*`.
      - Impact: `deny.toml` has `multiple-versions = "warn"` and `wildcards = "allow"`, so nothing fails.
      - Fix: upgrade in controlled steps. The `schemars` 1.x jump changes the JSON schema output and needs `schema_guard_test` review. Tighten `deny.toml` to deny wildcards. Effort M.
  
  11. **Dead and unused dependencies.**
      - Evidence: `cargo machete` flags `path-slash` in `callisto-cli`. The workspace declares `fs2` (`Cargo.toml`, `[workspace.dependencies]`) with no users in `crates/*`. Machete and mutants are justfile-only, not in CI.
      - Fix: remove them and add `just machete` to CI. Effort S.
  
  12. **No scheduled advisory scan, and Cargo updates are not automated.**
      - Evidence: workflows have no `schedule:` trigger, and `.github/dependabot.yml` covers only `github-actions`. `cargo deny` runs only on push or PR.
      - Impact: a published CLI should learn about a new RUSTSEC advisory without needing a PR. There is also no Cargo dependency update path.
      - Fix: add a weekly `cargo deny check advisories` job, and a `cargo` ecosystem in dependabot with `cooldown`. Effort S.
  
  13. **Release binary hardening is thin.**
      - Evidence: the release profile has `lto`, `codegen-units = 1` and `strip`. Beyond that there is no `panic = "abort"` decision, no `cargo-auditable` (embeds the dependency SBOM in the binary) [mem], no `--remap-path-prefix`, and `cargo install cross` runs unpinned by lockfile at release time (`.github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh:41`, pinned by `--version 0.2.5`, fine). Targets are macOS arm64, Linux gnu and Linux musl only.
      - Fix: consider `cargo auditable build`. Treat build-from-source reproducibility as a stated non-goal or document it. Windows and macOS x86_64 are product decisions, not Rust hygiene. Effort S to M.
  
  14. **Fuzzing is thin and not in CI.**
      - Evidence: `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` has 2 targets (`parse_changeset`, `parse_package_id`). The manifest parsers (Cargo, npm, pyproject) and `pre.json` are untrusted-input surfaces with no fuzz target.
      - Fix: add targets for the manifest editors and version parsers, and a short scheduled fuzz run. Effort M.
  
  15. **Smaller items.**
      - `deny.toml` allows `AGPL-3.0-only`, unused and unjustified for an FSL project. Remove it.
      - `#![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]` appears in `crates/callisto-cli/src/lib.rs:3`, `main.rs:1` and `callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:3`. This is a crate-wide silence of a real lint; box the large errors instead.
      - `just test` runs `cargo nextest run --workspace` without `--locked`. Add `--locked` to CI.
      - The commented per-crate coverage check is non-blocking (`callisto-ci.yml`), as the file itself says.
      - Effort S each.
  
  ### What the repo already does better than typical
  
  - **Workflow hygiene.** `zizmor` and `actionlint` run in CI. All actions are pinned by SHA with a `verify-action-pins.sh` check. Dependabot cooldown is set, and `persist-credentials: false` is used throughout. The release workflow has least-privilege `permissions`.
  - **Provenance.** Release assets get SLSA build provenance via `actions/attest-build-provenance`. A CI job verifies the latest release with `gh attestation verify`, `--signer-workflow` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`, including a tampered-copy negative control (`callisto-ci.yml`, `release-asset-attestation`).
  - **Release design.** There is a recoverable, idempotent, intent-bound pipeline: plan, build, then execute with a sha256-checked handoff.
  - **Lint baseline.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` and `[workspace.lints]` inheritance (`lints.workspace = true` in every crate). `let_underscore_must_use`, `map_err_ignore` and `unused_must_use` are denied.
  - **Error design.** `thiserror` plus `miette::Diagnostic` with stable codes and help text on `ModelError`.
  - **Process safety.** `Command::new` is used with argv arrays, no shell. Git calls use `--` separators; I saw `hash-object`, `log`, `tag` and `grep`, but `git grep` passes `rev` before `--` (`callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:411`), which I did not trace.   - **previous-tag-templates [REPRODUCED].** Packages `a` and `b` both declaring `old@{version}` both adopt `old@1.0.0`. That is explicit and name-only by design. A custom `tag-template` has no fallback, which is also by design.
  
  Cause and the other consumers of the tag index:
  - **Ownership gate** [SOURCE tags.rs:184-210]. It requires `pkg.id.ecosystem().is_some()`. The candidate list also requires a prefixed id.
  - **`sole_owner_at`** [SOURCE history.rs:93-103]. It returns the first candidate whose first manifest path exists at the rev, with no name check.
  - **pre.json** [SOURCE lib.rs:323-334]. The first `find(pre_json_key == key)` returns a bare package with no history check. It also calls `commit_adding` once per key inside the loop.
  - **`version_is_tagged` / `tag_of_version`** [SOURCE release_decision.rs:256-272]. The first branch, `contains_tag(template.render(V))`, is a raw name check (this is S3b). The second branch uses `last_tag`.

    - `aggregate.rs:230-262`: the `auto` inference window and `has_prior_release`.
    - `aggregate.rs:367`: the changelog `from`.
    - `groups.rs:30-36,132`: fixed-group alignment.
    - `status.rs:114` and `init.rs:259`.

  - **`releases_tagged_at`** [SOURCE release_decision.rs:283-298]. It matches the exact planned tag name at HEAD, which is ADR 9 adoption. Out of scope.
  
  ## 2. Design
  
  **Candidates for an unqualified tag `n@V`:** every package with a canonical manifest whose own name is `n`. This replaces `same`, which was prefixed ids with `id.name() == n`. `IdentityIndex::native_name` and `resolve_native` already provide the lookup.
  
  **Ownership key:** `(ecosystem, native name)`, with directory ignored.
  
  **Rule** (one function, `history::owner_at`, replacing `sole_owner_at`):
  1. Fast path. A candidate is a hit if any of its canonical manifests exists at `rev` and declares name `n` there. Declared names are read with `read_at` + `read_identity` and compared with `names_equal` in that manifest's ecosystem. Previously only the first manifest's path was checked, with no name check. One hit is the owner. Two or more hits is no owner.
  2. No hit. Take the existing roster, the ecosystems that declared `n` at `rev` (git grep plus manifest read, cached per `(rev, name)`). Owners are candidates with a native name `n` in one of those ecosystems. Exactly one is the owner, otherwise none.
  
  Check against the repros: S3, S5 and S6 find no owner and nothing is adopted. S7 has zero fast-path hits, the roster gives `{cargo}`, and `cargo/foo` wins.
  
  **Where it applies:**
  - Every default-template package that falls back to an unqualified `n@*` tag, bare or promoted. The `ecosystem().is_some()` guard is dropped.
  - The exact-tag check in `tag_of_version`. Verify the rendered tag only when `last_tag(P).version != V`. This is the backport and foreign case, so it costs nothing in the normal path.
  - G2. For a bare key whose bare package exists, call `owner_at` at the commit that added `pre.json`. If the owner is not that package, ignore the key, like an unknown key.   - `version_is_tagged` gets git access. Its callers (`derive_release_roster`, `derive.rs:787`) already have the workspace.
  
  **Selection order:** newest-first and lazy. Call `select_last_tag`, verify the chosen tag, and on rejection drop it and repeat. Do not verify every tag; ADR 11 costs one probe per candidate tag, which is too much for 200 bare packages.
  
  **Git cost.** `path_exists_at` is one `rev-parse`; `read_at` is two calls on a hit and one on a miss. A roster costs three `git grep` calls plus two per matching file, cached per `(rev, name)`.
  - Hot path: 2 spawns per bare package with a tag.
  - Measured spawn [REPRODUCED]: about 9.4 ms. Baseline `status` on the 200-package q200 repo with no tags: 0.11 s.
  - Estimate [not measured]: about +3.8 s for 200 bare packages.
  - Mitigation (second slice): `GitAccess::read_many_at` over `git cat-file --batch`, using `CommandRunner::run_with_stdin` (implemented in `callisto-cli/src/runner.rs:220`, currently unused).   - Message: "`foo@1.0.0` was made when `foo` named a manifest in npm; not adopted. If the package that made it was renamed, set `previous-tag-templates = [\"foo@{version}\"]` on its `[[package]]` rule."

  - Code: add `DiagnosticCode::TagOwnedByAnotherPackage` (`tag-owned-by-another-package`) in `callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs`, and add it to the expected set in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs:504`.   - It misfires on maintenance branches. Tags are global, so `release/1.x` at 1.5.0 sees `foo@2.0.0`.

  - **S3b** — `callisto release --dry-run` still plans cargo `foo` 0.1.0 after the rename. Old: omitted.

  - The fake runners assert `args == ["tag","--list"]` and will panic on the new probes. They are in `cascade/tests.rs:80`, `tags.rs:354`, `tests/tag_glob_cache_count_test.rs:69`, `tests/tags_laziness_test.rs:29` and `tests/snapshot_tests.rs:314`.

  - **`docs/specs/workspace.json` WS-ID-03.**
    - Replace the "last tag also found among `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its manifest and no other same-named package's" sentence with the new rule.

  - **New WS-ID-11.** The ownership rule, including the manifest name at the tag commit and an unrelated lookalike gaining no history.
  - **New WS-ID-12.** The `status` Info diagnostic.
  - **A criterion in `docs/specs/release.json`** (ID per that file's convention): a package whose `name@version` tag belongs to another package is still planned as unreleased.
  - **`docs/architecture/identity.md` "Historical ownership".** Rewrite it for the new rule. Document the `(ecosystem, native name)` key, the explicit `previous-tag-templates` route for a native rename, and the demotion note.
  - **ADR 11.** Correct the Consequences cost line ("one `git rev-parse` per candidate tag of a promoted package") and Enforcement. This is an existing-contract repair, so no new ADR.
  - **`docs/config.md`.** Add a note on `previous-tag-templates`: it is name-only, and it is the route for a native rename.
  - **Changeset.** `callisto add --package callisto-cli:patch`, written as what the user sees: "A package no longer adopts another package's `name@version` tags or its pre-release baseline."
  
  ## 5. PR slicing
  
  Use `gh stack`, per the memory note.
  
  | PR | Contents | Size |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | A | The `owner_at` name check and the generalized candidate set (S7), plus G2. No hot-path cost. | S |
  | B | Gate bare and promoted default-template tag adoption (S3, S5, S6), the `version_is_tagged` exact-tag check (S3b), the diagnostic, specs, docs, fixture churn. | M, close to L because of the fixture churn |
  | C | Batched `cat-file --batch` reads. Do it only if q200 with tags measures above about 1 s. | S-M |
  
  ## 6. Residual owner decisions
  
  1. **Empty roster at the tag commit** (no manifest anywhere declares `n`). Either strict: no history, with `previous-tag-templates` as the route. Or fail-open: adopt, as today. I recommend strict. Fail-open would cut fixture churn but re-opens name-only adoption for hand-made tags.
  2. **G2, a bare key the lone bare package did not own.** Either ignore, as unknown keys are today (recommended; the plan stays correct), or a new E316. I recommend ignore.
  3. **Diagnostic severity.** Either Info (recommended), or Warning, which strict mode could escalate.
  4. **Deleted-and-recreated same-ecosystem name** (S8 and S8b). Either the new package inherits (recommended, same registry identity). Or require path continuity, which would also break plain directory moves.
  5. **Cost.** Either ship per-call first and measure, or require batching in PR B.
  6. **The "last greater than current" guard.** Either skip it (recommended), or add it as Info only.
  
  ## 7. Not verified
  
  - Real timings of the new code. The +3.8 s figure is a spawn-count estimate.
  - `cat-file --batch` through the real runner, and fake-runner fallback.
  - Blobless and shallow behavior beyond my small test. Reading a blob at a tag worked in a depth-1 clone with a fetched tag, and in a `--filter=blob:none` clone (lazy fetch). A `git grep` roster in a blobless clone could fetch many blobs; I did not test it.
  - The `auto`-trigger inference effect of S3 (source only).
  - Non-dry-run `release` after the fix, and the `init` Detected output.
  - Behavior of Python names with the first-word grep needle in the new fast path.
  - Exact count of unit tests needing fixtures.

  # Callisto 1.0 publishing: practice and competition review (2026-10-20)
  
  Read-only. Repo facts cite paths in the v1-research worktree. External facts cite URLs; items I could not confirm are marked (unverified) and listed in section 6.
  
  ## 1. Headline
  
  The 2026 norm is tokenless publishing on all three registries. Callisto still requires long-lived secrets, and its own policy check forbids the alternative. This is the one 1.0-blocking expectation. Callisto's execution model (committed decision, observe-and-adopt reruns) is strong. Its supply-chain surface lags: no registry OIDC, no PyPI attestations, no checksum sidecars, and a first-publish story that is undocumented.
  
  ## 2. A. Secure publishing: practice vs Callisto
  
  | Practice (norm) | Callisto today | Gap |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | crates.io Trusted Publishing: OIDC exchange for a short-lived token via [crates-io-auth-action](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action). Needs `id-token: write`. The first publish must be manual ([RFC 3691](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/3691-trusted-publishing-cratesio.html), [blog 2025-07](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07)). GitLab was added, plus a "trusted-publishing-only" crate setting, and `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` are blocked ([blog 2026-01](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/01/21/crates-io-development-update)). | `execute` uses `secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `docs/publishing.md`). | OIDC absent. |
  | npm trusted publishing: npm CLI 11.5.1+, `id-token: write`, provenance automatic, GitHub-hosted/GitLab/CircleCI ([docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers)). Classic tokens were revoked 2025-12-09 and write granular tokens capped at 90 days ([GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-12-09-npm-classic-tokens-revoked-session-based-auth-and-cli-token-management-now-available/)). `npm trust` (11.15+) only works on packages that already exist ([docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-trust)). SlugFest (disclosed 2026-10-13): configs bound to repo slug, not ID. Unvalidated configs now expire after 48h ([WorkOS write-up](https://workos.com/blog/npm-trusted-publishing-slugfest)). | The docs' main path is an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Provenance is opt-in via `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` plus `id-token` (`docs/publishing.md:56`). The generated workflow's `execute` job already has `id-token: write` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:220`). | The generated workflow always injects `NPM_TOKEN`. CI has a tamper negative control (`callisto-ci.yml:216-265`). Strong. | The SLSA level is not documented. Registry publishes are not attested, except npm if the user opts in. |

  ### Policy conflict (verified in code)
  
  `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh` sets `OIDC_JOBS = {"build-artifact"}` and `ALLOWED_WRITES["execute"] = {"contents"}`. It requires the set of secrets referenced in `execute` to equal exactly `{CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN}`. Its self-test mutation "id-token on execute" must fail. Consequences:
  
  - Callisto's own workflow cannot adopt crates.io trusted publishing without editing the script.
  - A tokenless `execute` (zero secrets) also fails the script.
  - The written rule in AGENTS.md ("only `execute` gets registry secrets", no Environment or reviewer gate) does not forbid OIDC in `execute`. The `id-token` ban lives only in the script.
